LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights How to watch the 'Thursday Night Football' matchup, plus a preview and prediction Patrick Smith/Getty Images In the Week 10 edition of "Thursday Night Football," the New York Giants play host to the division rival Washington Commanders . New York enters this game riding high atop the NFC East, having won each of its last two games sandwiching a Week 8 bye. The Giants are surprisingly in the playoff picture in the first year of the John Harbaugh era despite losing starting quarterback Jaxson Dart in Week 2. They recently turned to J.J. McCarthy in place of Jameis Winston but kept on winning. Washington climbed out of last place in the NFC East thanks to a Week 8 win over the lowly Philadelphia Eagles but still has the second-worst record in the conference. The Commanders missed an opportunity for a win the last time these two teams played by mismanaging the clock as poorly as any team ever has, and they will surely be looking to atone for that mistake here. Will the Giants keep rolling, or will the Commanders capture a rare victory? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game. Where to watch Giants vs. Commanders live Date: Thursday, Nov. 12 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Location: MetLife Stadium (East Rutherford, New Jersey) Streaming: Amazon Prime Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Giants -2.5, O/U 40.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Commanders have the ball The Commanders are not particularly effective either passing or running the football. They rank 21st in the NFL in net yards per pass attempt (which accounts for yards lost to sacks), and they're 23rd in designed rushing yards per carry, which eliminates scrambling from the picture. Their most effective form of offense is scrambling, where Jayden Daniels and Marcus Mariota have run 29 times for 274 yards — the most scramble yards in the NFL, per Tru Media. But that's not something that you can lean on down-to-down. Daniels has completed only 63.9% of his passes at an average of 6.9 yards per attempt. While he has seven passing touchdowns and has yet to be intercepted, he has a low passing success rate (43.9%, according to Tru Media), has generated explosives at only an average rate (7.8%) and has struggled on third downs (30.9%). Again, his most effective way of moving the ball has been via the scramble. The Giants are actually second in the NFL in passing success rate allowed and third in explosives per dropback, according to Tru Media. So Daniels, with his limited receiving corps in the absence of Terry McLaurin , might find it difficult to move the ball through the air. The Giants, though, have been vulnerable to opponent scrambles, allowing quarterbacks to take off downfield on a league-high 23.9% of pressured dropbacks and yielding 225 scramble yards to date. So Daniels could have some room to run. In the absence of Jacory Croskey-Merritt , the Commies have turned to Rachaad White and Austin Ekeler in the backfield. They have not been particularly effective on the ground, but they're each capable outlet receivers for Daniels, who has targeted backs on 14.4% of his passes, a slightly higher rate than last year (12.8%). Doing so against the Giants may not be the most advisable strategy, though, because it means testing rookie linebacker Arvell Reese in space, and Reese has been a space-eating demon so far this season. Daniels' other pass-catchers at the moment are Stefon Diggs , Antonio Williams , Van Jefferson and Chig Okonkwo. The Giants have been good at limiting tight ends over the middle (there's Reese showing up again), so the passing game might run through the perimeter receivers, who will face off with an improved Deonte Banks and the recently-extended Greg Newsome II on the outside. Look for Daniels to at least try to test those guys deep down the field, given he has the seventh-highest deep throw rate among qualified quarterbacks. The Giants have faced deep passes at essentially an average rate so far this season, and they've been excellent at defending them, checking in second in EPA per dropback on those plays. Still, dinking and dunking hasn't been all that effective for Daniels and the Commanders, so they're going to have to try to hit on a few big plays. When the Giants have the ball The Giants turned to J.J. McCarthy as their quarterback in garbage time of their loss to the Saints back in Week 6, and they have stuck with him over the last two games. They've been a somewhat unusual offense with McCarthy under center. McCarthy himself has not been efficient on a down-to-down basis. He's completed only 63.2% of his passes, and he has one touchdown pass and one interception. He checks in 31st in success rate among 37 quarterbacks with at least 75 dropbacks this season, according to Tru Media. But McCarthy is averaging 9.1 (!!!!) yards per attempt, and he's 15th among the same group of 37 quarterbacks in EPA per dropback. That's because when he does complete passes, they're basically all going for big gains in big situations. He's throwing the ball farther downfield than anyone in the league (10.6-yard average depth of target), and he's leading the NFL in explosive plays per dropback at 16.0%, per Tru Media. The Commanders' defense is essentially the opposite of what McCarthy has done so far. They yield a high passing success rate (21st in the league) but a low explosive rate (11th). The tension between those two poles will be interesting to watch play out on Monday night. When McCarthy drops back to pass, he is looking most often to Malik Nabers , who has been the intended receiver on 31.7% of McCarthy's throws. Malachi Fields , not Isaiah Likely , has been the secondary target, with a 20.6% target share compared to Likely's 17.5% rate. Before McCarthy took over at quarterback, Likely tied Nabers for the team lead in target share at 29.4%, compared to just 11.2% for Fields. Nabers and Fields will do most of their work against Rasul Douglas and Amik Robertson on the outside, while Likely will see a lot of rookie linebacker Sonny Styles , slot corner Mike Sainristil and safeties Jeremy Reaves and Nick Cross . The Commanders have not generated very much pressure this season (33.5% of opponent dropbacks, per Tru Media, 25th in the league), while McCarthy has been one of the league's most-pressured quarterbacks since taking over. He tends to hold the ball for a while as he looks to push it down the field. Whether the Commanders can get after him will go a long way toward determining whether he can complete any big plays. Cam Skattebo is back for the Giants in this game, and he's likely to take over the lead role from Devin Singletary , who struggled last week and is more suited to being a passing-down back. Skattebo hasn't been very effective as a rusher this season, averaging 4.3 yards per carry with a 45.9% success rate, but he had his best game of the year before sitting out last week after the bye. The Commanders have been solid against the run, yielding only 3.9 yards per carry, with below-average marks both before (1.09) and after contact (2.83). This might be a game where the Giants lean on those big plays from McCarthy. I don't feel particularly comfortable predicting that this Giants team will improve to 6-2-1, but I just don't have much faith this version of Washington can be all that competitive either. The Commanders can't run the ball right now and have to lean on a passing game that hasn't been all that efficient. The Giants haven't exactly looked like world beaters this year (four of their five wins have come in one-score games), and they definitely didn't look great against the Eagles last week, but I think they can get it done on Thursday night. TOP Pick Commanders vs Giants prediction: Commanders +2.5 The Washington Commanders aren't as bad as their 2-5-1 record might lead you to believe, and the New York Giants aren't as good as their 5-2-1 record might indicate. Washington went down to the wire with the Rams in Week 9, losing a close game while gaining more yards per play than L.A. Two games before that, the Commanders lost by six in San Francisco, but were competitive enough to cover the spread. They've shown plenty of fight against good competition and tied these Giants in Week 5 , but probably should've won after winning the yards-per-play battle 6.3 to 4.9 . Wet, chilly weather is expected, which could make Washington's biggest advantage even more important: the ground game. It ranks eighth in yards per rush against a Giants defense ranked 27th in yards per rush allowed . Throw in a sketchy quarterback situation, with J.J. picks.blurb: NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 10 NFL updates Maye, Hutchinson injured College football winners/losers Week 10 Fantasy Football Toolkit: Start/sit advice, rankings, sleepers, more UFC 334 takeaways NFL predictions: Our picks for Giants-Commanders, the full Week 10 slate The Giants and Commanders played to a draw five weeks ago. Who wll win this time? | Getty Images Ed Valentine · SB Nation Thu, November 12, 2026 at 5:00 PM UTC · 6 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The New York Giants and Washington Commanders kick off Week 10 of the NFL season Thursday night at what promises to be a rainy, chilly MetLife Stadium. Can the Giants solidify their NFC East lead, or will the race for the division title tighten? Here is how the Big Blue View staff sees that game, and the rest of the Week 10 matchups. Which version of the Giants will show up on Thursday night? Will we get the sloppy Giants that came out flat against the Philadelphia Eagles, or the tough, physical, and technically sound Giants that showed up against the Houston Texans? John Harbaugh's 9-1 record home record on Thursday Nights is encouraging. I would say that this is a game the Giants should win on paper, particularly with Washington missing some of their best players and their starting center in the concussion protocol. However, I'm also not convinced that these Giants can play a normal game and just take care of business. I keep waiting for the Giants to play a complete game and execute on offense and defense, but this team seems unable to be both consistent and explosive. I hope the offensive line comes prepared to bully an injured Washington defensive line and J.J. McCarthy isn't forced into low percentage throws every third down by long yardage situations. Likewise, I hope that Dennard Wilson comes out swinging on defense, but also has a counterpunch ready in case Jayden Daniels has an answer to the Cover-0 blitz. I'm picking the Giants here, but they can't afford to take Washington lightly or give Jayden Daniels the chance to catch his breath and swing the game. Tony Del Genio This is the Giants' second consecutive must-win game. You wouldn't think that when 5-2-1 plays 2-5-1, but (1) the Giants haven't beaten the Commanders since Jayden Daniels became their quarterback (even though Daniels didn't play in one of those losses), (2) despite their record, Washington has beaten the Seahawks and only narrowly lost to the 49ers and Rams while the Giants were beaten soundly by the Rams, the only good team they've faced, and still have the 49ers and Seahawks coming up, along with the Jaguars and Lions. A division loss greatly weakens their hold on the NFC East lead, their only real path to the playoffs. Terry McLaurin is out for the season, but in his place is Stefon Diggs, who did not face the Giants in the first game. Jacory Crosky-Merritt, who beat the Giants' run D for a 33-yard TD right off the bat in the first game, is also out. The Commanders are further decimated by injuries since their last meeting to key starters such as DT Daron Payne and IOL Lucas Patrick. So really the Giants should prevail. The problem is…containing the running of Daniels, which they did not do well in their first meeting (103 yards, by far his highest of the season, and his only 2 rushing TDs of the season). Hopefully Dennard Wilson will have a plan for that. If so, and if the Giants execute it, then the Giants can win. David Hartman The rematch of the NFL's only tie game of the season will be played in prime time on Thursday night, and for the ninth time in nine games, the Giants are playing a team that doesn't have a winning record. But you can throw the records out the window: The 5-2-1 Giants, at home, are just 1.5 point favorites over the 2-5-1 Commanders. Go figure… Big Blue won with defense and a strong kicking game on Sunday in Philadelphia, with Arvel Reese perhaps becoming a star in real time. It was an ugly win, with the offense producing just 19 points. The Giants will need more than that against Jayden Daniels and company on Thursday night. Cam Skattebo is expected back, and that's good news. New York couldn't run the ball on Sunday, which stagnated their offense. Right tackle Jermaine Eluemunor (calf) might miss this game, however, and the O-line struggled at Philadelphia as it was. J.J. McCarthy wasn't terrible on Sunday, but he wasn't especially good either and now he's dealing with a hip pointer. Jameis Winston led New York on its only touchdown drive while McCarthy was temporarily knocked from the game. McCarthy hasn't thrown a TD pass (or an interception) in either of his two starts. This figures to be a close game, just like the first one. It'll be fun to watch standout rookies Reese and Sonny Styles — college teammates at Ohio State last season — leading the way for each defense. Seriously – how did anyone score on the Buckeyes? Anyway, Dennard Wilson needs to find a way to keep Daniels from gashing his defense with his legs. He ran for 103 yards and two scores in the first game. This game could come down to intangibles like turnovers and special teams. The G-Men have been winning (or tying) close games and that's a reflection on good coaching to a degree, and favorable luck. In a game that should be close, who am I to pick against that? Pick: Giants in a squeaker Valentine's View We are not picking games by the spread here, but I am surprised the Giants are just 1.5-point favorites. That indicates a continuing lack of real belief in the Giants in the betting market. The Giants understand the opportunity they have in front of them, and how important this game is. In the rainy, windy, miserable conditions at MetLife Stadium Thursday evening I think you have to expect what has become a typical Giants game this season — close, somewhat sloppy, decided by who makes the plays and who properly handles the situations at the end of the game. I have far more faith in the Giants to do that than I do the Commanders. We all remember the Commanders stunning clock mismanagement at the end of the Week 5 tie with the Giants. That sort of questionable decision-making has continued to plague Washington, which is 1-3-1 in games decided by one score. If you could the Arizona game, which I do since it was decided on the game's final play, seven of the Giants eight games this season were one-score games. The Giants are 5-1-1 in those games. They have lived on the edge, and have shown an ability to survive. Is that formula sustainable forever? Maybe not. It does, though, make me feel good about the Giants' chances on Thursday. However, Nabers hasn't held an injury designation in multiple weeks, and that's the case once again on Thursday night against the Washington Commanders. Nabers was able to log a few "full" practices in the lead up to Thursday's game, and he should have a massive role for the Giants' offense. New York is off a 5-2-1 start this season, and Nabers put on a show in a tie against Washington back in Week 5. He caught 11 of his 20 targets for 121 yards and a score to pace the New York offense. With J.J. McCarthy now at quarterback for New York, Nabers has a slightly higher ceiling than he did with Jameis Winston. Overall, the former first-round pick has 53 catches for 648 yards and two scores through the first half of the regular season. Can he keep things going on Thursday? The Lions come into the international matchup at 6-2 and are coming off a 19-9 win over the Miami Dolphins . The victory extended their win streak to four games. Detroit's 6-2 record is strong, but because the NFC North is so good, they are currently narrowly in second place in the division, tied record-wise with the Minnesota Vikings . The Patriots story is a bit different, coming off a bad loss to the Green Bay Packers . In the 45-27 defeat, quarterback Drake Maye threw three interceptions, tying him with winless Los Angeles Chargers QB Justin Herbert for most picks in the league (11). The Patriots are 2-2 in their last four games and sit in second place in the AFC East. Both teams can make big plays, but it's what happens between those big gains that may determine the winner of this matchup between two coaches, Mike Vrabel and Dan Campbell, who tend to be aggressive in their play-calling. Lions vs. Patriots need to know Injuries: The Patriots will be without CB Carlton Davis III (knee), C/G Ben Brown (knee) and RB TreVeyon Henderson (illness) this week and nine other players are questionable, including WR A.J. Brown (ankle/knee), RB Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) and S Kevin Byard III (chest). Brown, who has missed the last two weeks and was IR earlier this season, returned to practice this week in a limited capacity. Brown's production in the three games he did play didn't live up to his hype, drawing criticism from fans. If he can play, all eyes will be on him, especially with the team having fewer options in the run game. Defenses: The Lions' defense has improved over the last few weeks, allowing 15.5 points per game in its last four matchups, after being near the bottom of the league in many categories, including yards allowed per game (423.8) in the first four weeks. The Patriots defense got embarrassed last week, with arguably Christian Gonzalez's worst game of his career. New England's defense has allowed the eighth most passing yards per game (231.9). The team does significantly better against the run, landing eighth-best (96.7), right behind the Lions' run defense (94.1). The Lions offense is top 10 in the league, thanks to Jaymyr Gibbs, who already has 847 yards on the ground and will present a challenge for the Patriots. The Lions' pass defense is still at the bottom in terms of yards allowed (260.9), and with the Patriots needing to improve and establish their air game, this would be the chance to try and expose Detroit's weakness. Pass game: The Patriots' passing game pales in comparison to their Week 10 opponent's. Lions wide receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown has 61 receptions for 657 receiving yards, more than the Patriots' top two WRs ( DeMario Douglas , Efton Chism III ) combined. The lack of production is in part due to struggles from quarterback Drake Maye and the absence of a true WR1, with Brown missing most games and the loss of Kayshon Boutte this offseason. St. Brown's mom is from Germany and it will be the first game he plays on German soil, which should only increase his excitement and production. International history: This marks the sixth regular-season game to be held in Germany and the third played in Munich. It marks the final European game of the season. The NFL traveled to Germany last season as well, when the Colts and Falcons met in November at the Olympic Stadium. Detroit Lions president & CEO Rod Wood expressed his excitement to be playing in Germany, saying , "We are thrilled to be playing internationally and specifically in Munich for the 2026 season. As an organization, we have invested greatly in the German market and are excited to play in front of our passionate German fans." This game could really go either way and we will know if the Patriots offense has the juice to win right away, as their first few drives tend to establish the rest of the game. If New England's defense can bounce back and Maye can stop giving the ball away, they can keep themselves in the playoff conversation with a win. away.headline: A.J. Brown injury update as Patriots WR hurt again vs. Lions
away.blurb: The Patriots announced on social media that Brown is questionable to return to the Week 10 game in Munich with a hamstring injury. The Fox broadcast showed Brown walking back to the locker room with a trainer early in the fourth quarter of New England's clash with the Detroit Lions . Brown's presence in the game in Germany marked his first appearance since Week 7 . The wideout had been dealing with ankle and knee injuries that knocked him out of Weeks 8 and 9. Brown had also previously missed four games earlier this season with a high ankle sprain he sustained during Week 1. The Patriots ' star wide receiver sustained a hamstring injury in the final minutes of the third quarter in Week 10. Brown is considered questionable to return, according to the team. The wideout, whom the Patriots acquired for a 2027 fifth-round pick and a 2028 first-round pick, has appeared in two full games for New England so far. Brown exited Week 1's clash with the Seattle Seahawks early with a high ankle sprain. His return in Week 6 lasted two games, then knee and ankle injuries kept him out for Weeks 8 and 9. Two quarters after the reigning AFC champions lost quarterback Drake Maye to an ankle injury , they've also lost wide receiver A.J. Brown . Before his departure, Brown had two catches for 27 yards on six targets. Brown appears to have suffered his leg injury after catching a 21-yard pass on a third-and-3 play that was his second reception of the day. He went to the blue medical tent on New England's sideline after the play and was later spotted heading back to the locker room with a team trainer. Brown returned in Week 10, but he was unable to make it through the game in Munich after sustaining the hamstring injury.

away.headline: Drake Maye injury update as Patriots QB goes to locker room
away.blurb: Maye, who never returned to action, was officially ruled out with about six minutes left to play in the first half. Maye and his team may have caught something of a break, depending on the severity of his injury. The Patriots enter their bye week upon their return from Germany, which will provide their quarterback extra time to recuperate. The New England Patriots will be without their most important player for the remainder of Sunday's game in Germany. On a costly play for both teams, Pats quarterback Drake Maye and Detroit Lions defensive end Aidan Hutchinson were both hurt on the opening drive of their clubs' matchup in Munich on Sunday, Nov. 15. Five-and-a-half minutes into the NFL 's final game in Europe this year, Maye, the runner-up for league MVP honors in 2025, suffered an ankle injury on a sack by Hutchinson − who was hurt while celebrating the play . Hutchinson pulled Maye down to the ground on the play and leapt in the air to celebrate the play, but he recoiled as his knee seemed to buckle when he landed. Maye, meanwhile, was doubled over on the sideline after the play while the Patriots kicked a field goal following the sequence. Backup quarterback Tommy DeVito entered the game on New England's subsequent position as Maye walked gingerly to the locker room. Hutchinson also left the field for medical attention. Better known as "Tommy Cutlets," the New Jersey native rose to prominence as an undrafted rookie with the New York Giants in 2023, when he wound up starting six games and played surprisingly well. The Patriots claimed DeVito off waivers prior to the start of the 2025 campaign and kept him as their third-string quarterback behind Maye and Joshua Dobbs. DeVito signed a two-year, $7.4 million contract in March and became Maye's primary backstop later in the month, when Dobbs was released. (Ironically, Dobbs now backs up Lions QB Jared Goff.) Prior to Sunday, DeVito had played sparingly with New England. He didn't play a single snap in 2025 and had thrown eight passes in two brief appearances this season prior to Sunday. Fox rules analyst Mike Pereira, formerly the NFL's vice president of officiating, said Hutchinson was not guilty of a hip-drop tackle on the play, and no flag was thrown after it. Atlanta has lost four of its last five games and is coming off a disappointing performance against the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid. Now, the Falcons will have to find a way to slow down another talented quarterback while dealing with significant changes to their own roster. Kansas City will enter the matchup without running back Kenneth Walker III , which could make things more manageable for Atlanta’s struggling defense. However, Mahomes and Travis Kelce remain major threats, and the Chiefs have plenty of weapons to exploit the Falcons’ defensive weaknesses and deficiencies. How will the game play out? The FalconsSI staff delivers its weekly predictions. Scott Kennedy (4-5) The Falcons have had some frustrating games this year, suffering through two weeks of Cooper Rush and a monsoon in Tampa, for example. But last week in Madrid was different. The Cincinnati Bengals simply showed the Falcons aren't good enough this year. Their defense has been patched together with duct tape and one-year contracts, and it simply couldn't hold up against Joe Burrow, Ja'Marr Chase, and Tee Higgins. General manager Ian Cunningham saw the same thing we did, and rather than deluding himself into thinking 3-6 in a weak NFC South was good enough, he sold at the trade deadline. Now Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce come to Mercedes-Benz Stadium, and the Falcons are without All-Pro safety Jessie Bates III after trading him to the Jaguars. Mahomes and the Chiefs aren't as explosive as the Bengals, but, well, they're still Mahomes and the Chiefs... and they're better on defense. We'll see if Michael Penix Jr. and the offense can play well enough to take another step towards feeling good about Penix in 2027, but the Falcons are staring 3-7 in the face. Prediction: Chiefs 31, Falcons 17 Gerald Thomas, III (4-5) The notion of the Falcons playing up to the competition is fading away. Plus, there’s a belief that Atlanta is now playing for draft positioning instead of ending its playoff drought. The Chiefs present too many issues for the Falcons. We all know what Patrick Mahomes can do in the passing attack. And we all watched the Atlanta secondary struggle with Bengals playmakers in Madrid. With Kenneth Walker III out, that may soften the blow against the Falcons’ dwindling run defense . Offensively, Atlanta is looking pretty “eh.” Michael Penix Jr. has gotten off of his heater and must prove himself as the franchise quarterback against one of the top pass defenses in the league. Additionally, Kansas City is top-10 at stopping the run and will likely stack boxes to stonewall Bijan Robinson as the Falcons deal with the key loss of powerback Brian Robinson Jr. Atlanta is looking at a third consecutive loss on the road to the 2027 NFL Draft. Prediction: Chiefs 34, Falcons 21 Garrett Chapman (4-5) The Falcons have lost four of their last five, and the road to snapping that skid will run through the Kansas City Chiefs. The perennial contenders will be without Kenneth Walker, but Patrick Mahomes and Travis Kelce are still willing and able to run wild on a reeling Falcons defense that just moved Jessie Bates. On offense, Corey Levin will be taking over at center , and he'll have a pretty difficult challenge opposite him. This should be a tight game, but I'm not sure the Falcons can overcome this team opposite them right now. Prediction: Chiefs 20, Falcons 17 Darius Hayes (4-5) Expects a closer game with Walker sidelined, but Mahomes will ultimately make the difference. Atlanta’s defense has continued to struggle, and the departure of Bates doesn’t provide much confidence that things will improve against Kansas City’s passing attack. The Falcons also face questions offensively with a new starting center stepping into the lineup midway through the season. That transition could create additional problems against a talented Chiefs defense. Atlanta remains competitive, but Kansas City will pull away late to secure the victory. Prediction: Chiefs 23, Falcons 16 Jerry Jones, Falcons Podcast , (4-5) Despite being only a half game back from first place in the division, it really seems like the clock is ticking on the Falcons’ season. The performances in recent weeks and the trades the Falcons made at the deadline make this game feel like a “crap or get off the pot” moment for this team. There is hope, though. The Chiefs are good, but the Falcons have beaten better teams this year (which sounds crazy given they’ve only won three games). The blueprint for beating the Chiefs is pretty straightforward: stop the run. The issue is, the Falcons have struggled to do that, especially against inside runs, and the Chiefs are an inside-running team. If they can pull it off, the Falcons’ pass defense matches up well against the Chiefs’ passing offense on paper (even without Jessie Bates). On the other side of the ball, the Chiefs’ defense has been solid, but I think they have a real weakness in the secondary with the injury to their rookie Mansoor Delane. To exploit it, though, the Falcons will need to get the run game going. Their passing offense has been pretty ineffective when the ground game stalls. This is a game the Falcons can win... but whether they will is a different story. Prediction: Chiefs 24, Falcons 16 Final Predictions: Chiefs Are the Unanimous Pick Despite differences in the projected final scores, all five contributors are picking Kansas City to win in Week 10. The absence of Kenneth Walker could give Atlanta an opportunity to make this a more competitive matchup, but Mahomes remains the biggest difference-maker heading into Sunday. For the Falcons, the challenge will be finding a way to slow down Kansas City’s passing attack while getting enough production from Penix and the offense. Atlanta needs a win to stop its recent slide, but the consensus among our staff is that the Chiefs will leave Mercedes-Benz Stadium with another victory. Kickoff is set for 1:00 p.m. EST at Mercedes-Benz Stadium and will be shown on CBS. It's been mostly positive on the results front for the Kansas City Chiefs, who come into Sunday's game against the Atlanta Falcons sitting at a healthy 6-2 overall. Although Atlanta seems to be trending in the wrong direction, it's still in business to compete in a lackluster NFC South. Could that lead to an inspired home performance against visiting Kansas City, or will it be smooth sailing for head coach Andy Reid's group? With kickoff on the horizon, which side will come out on top today? The Kansas City Chiefs On SI crew makes its predictions for Week 10 of the regular season. Joshua Brisco: The loss of Kenneth Walker impacts how the Chiefs may choose to manage this game, but it shouldn’t change the final result. Kansas City still has the advantage on both sides of the ball, even though Atlanta has punched above its weight twice this season. Ultimately, I expect the Chiefs to navigate through a relatively tough game and return home with the win. Jordan Foote: Being down Walker undoubtedly could make life more difficult for the Chiefs, but rookie Emmett Johnson's been nothing short of awesome when on the field. Look for him to leave attempts at tackles behind on Sunday afternoon and factor into a passing game that has a less-than-100% Xavier Worthy but a new addition in Josh Downs. The real intrigue, in my view, comes on the defensive side. Can Steve Spagnuolo's unit find a way to slow down running back Bijan Robinson and wideout Drake London? If so, putting the fate of the game in quarterback Michael Penix Jr.'s hands seems like a losing formula for Atlanta. It may not be as pretty and resounding as Week 9's throttling of the Jets was, but it should be another victory regardless. Joshua Schulman: Coming off a much-needed bounce-back win at home, the Chiefs will hit the road against a perplexing Falcons squad. They have defeated the 49ers at home and put up 45 points on their division rival Saints on the road, yet they were also shut out by the Buccaneers in a four-interception outing from Michael Penix Jr. Ultimately, I think this will come down to the version of Atlanta that shows up. The Falcons rank in the bottom half of the league in both rushing and passing defense, so I’m expecting Emmett Johnson to wreak havoc on the ground despite Kenneth Walker’s absence. It’ll also be Josh Downs’ first appearance in the red and gold after he was acquired via trade from the Colts. I do think the threat of Bijan Robinson and being away from home will keep this close, but I have Kansas City pulling away in a narrow finish. Tyler Brown: Nothing like a Week 9 win against the Jets to trick the mind into thinking Kansas City turned the corner after an explosive second half, but that might be what happened. Setting aside the Harrison Butker and Josh Simmons drama, the Chiefs looked like an inspired team led by their old faithful stars. Travis Kelce and Chris Jones both posted big performances, and Rashee Rice and George Karlaftis are becoming key cogs in their respective units. A mid-season acquisition like Josh Downs can also provide a shot in the arm for a team. This game will be won in the trenches. Atlanta has Robinson, the NFL’s leading rusher, so the Chiefs’ defensive line and linebackers will need a big day to contain him. If they do, Penix, the worst quarterback in the league when facing pressure, will be forced to beat them. On the other side, Walker’s injury leaves the Chiefs’ rushing attack in question. With Kahlil Benson and Josh Ezeudu starting at tackle, the Chiefs will need a big day from Johnson. I think they get it done, kicking the Falcons while they’re down in the same week they traded away their best center and safety. Don’t get me wrong, Atlanta has a lot to play for, just a half-game back in a weak NFC South despite being 3-6. Cox/Getty Images) | Getty Images Jared Sapp · SB Nation Fri, November 13, 2026 at 9:30 PM UTC · 9 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads It's time for the Arrowhead Pride staff to put their opinions to the test. Before the Kansas City Chiefs travel to face the Atlanta Falcons , our writers predicted the final score and result. Atlanta has been an unpredictable team both looking dominant in their trio of wins while struggling in most of their six losses. FanDuel Sportsbook currently lists the Chiefs as 3.5-point home favorites. The Falcons also have the misfortune of not coming off of a European game into their bye week. The Falcons lost 34-17 to the Cincinnati Bengals in Madrid, Spain on Sunday. They also sent starting safety Jessie Bates to the Jacksonville Jaguars ahead of Tuesday's trade deadline. We also want to know your score prediction! Vote in the poll on The Feed and share your score prediction ! Jared Sapp ( @TrumanChief ) I do worry about the Falcons' pass rush, even if their defense's other two levels were underwhelming even before trading Bates. With the league's two best running backs facing off, I expect a run heavy day that should lead to a fast moving game. Look for the Chiefs' pass rush to build on their second half against Atlanta quarterback Michael Penix. This will be a game where Atlanta looks game for a couple of drives before the Chiefs overwhelm in route to a victory. The run game will lead to limited possessions for both sides to keep the scoring from getting out of hand. Chiefs 27, Falcons 17 Caleb James ( @CJScoobs ) The Chiefs and Falcons are on opposite ends of the competitive spectrum in the NFL, and this week's game should show that. The Falcons traded away veteran safety Jessie Bates to the contending Jacksonville Jaguars, while the Chiefs traded for wide receiver Josh Downs from the Indianapolis Colts. Despite a talented core of offensive playmakers, including Bijan Robinson and Drake London, the Falcons are only 3-6, largely because their defense allows over 340 yards per game. The Falcons are -8 in the turnover-takeaway category, 30th in the NFL, while the Chiefs are tied for 9th at +4. If they can force turnovers, they will be in good shape to win the game. I don't think Downs will play more than 20 snaps this week, but I would expect the Chiefs to design a few routes for him to get his feet wet in the offense. Chiefs 27, Falcons 13 Mark Gunnels ( @MarkAGunnels ) I've got the Chiefs winning this one. Josh Downs makes his debut, and I like Mahomes having another guy who can get open underneath, especially now that Atlanta traded away Jessie Bates. The Falcons also traded their starting center, Ryan Neuzil, so I expect Chris Jones to make life real uncomfortable up the middle. Chiefs 27, Falcons 20 Maurice Elston ( @MrMauriceElston ) What impressed me most about the Chiefs' 35–12 win over the Jets was how they finished. Kansas City has a habit of letting teams it should beat hang around, and the Jets were within two points at halftime. The Chiefs outscored them 21–0 from there. Kenneth Walker III looked like the player we saw during the 5–0 start, finishing with 143 yards from scrimmage and three touchdowns. To keep Walker rolling, the Chiefs need their receivers to win against man coverage. Seattle and Denver showed what happens when defenses can load the box and trust their corners to hold up one-on-one: the run slows down, and play-action loses its bite. If the receivers make Atlanta pay for that approach, Walker will have more room to run and Patrick Mahomes can get back to attacking off play-action. Against Atlanta, the key is slowing down Bijan Robinson. That's the operative phrase: slow him down. He's coming off 100 rushing yards and another 47 through the air, so Kansas City has to account for him even when he doesn't get the handoff. Drake London demands attention, and Kyle Pitts can still cause problems for the Chiefs' linebackers and safeties even in a quiet season. But if Kansas City's run defense keeps Robinson from taking over, Sack Nation can build on its five-sack performance by moving Michael Penix Jr. off his spot and forcing him past his first read. I like the Chiefs' chances when Atlanta has to win that way. Matt Stagner ( @stagdsp ) Your Kansas City Chiefs head to Atlanta as big favorites against the 2-6 Falcons. Yes, they've lost 4 of their last 5, but this is a dangerous opponent. They've got the league's best RB and a streaky young QB– it's an offense that can get out to an early lead and make things uncomfortable. But, as always, this game will come down to how the Chiefs execute. From the pass protection to the receivers and the short-yardage offense, this team has questions, but they're more than capable. Ideally, they start strong with Walker and Johnson– if the run game gets going, the Chiefs are hard to beat. Chiefs 33, Falcons 21 Dakota Watson ( @D_Watson56 ) The Chiefs enter this game after righting some of their wrongs last week against the Jets, although still with major question marks for a team intent on making a Super Bowl run. The Falcons, meanwhile, are on a two game losing skid after their upset win over the previously unbeaten San Francisco 49ers. I never quite know what to make of the Falcons. They're a team with some of the best offensive weapons in the entire NFL, yet they can't ever seem to put it all together. Since Jonathan Taylor in week 2, Bijan Robinson will be the best running back the Chiefs have faced all season. The Chiefs have been great defending the run in 2026, and I think they will be able to contain Robinson, but he will still get his yards. Defensively, the Chiefs should also be able to continue the positive momentum they established last week in pressuring the quarterback and leading to mistakes by the Falcons' offense. I'm excited to see what the Chiefs' offense has in store for new wide receiver Josh Downs. I'm keeping my expectations in check, however, as it always seems like the Chiefs onboard their wide receivers slowly. I expect Downs to play 35-50% of the team's snaps, but they will still be able to generate enough offense to take home the win. Rocky Magana ( @RockyMagana ) The Atlanta Falcons only show up for primetime games; they are garbage during noon kickoffs. Despite having multiple weapons on offense, namely running back Bijan Robinson and wide receiver Drake London, they can never seem to put it all together in the daytime. On the other hand, the Chiefs are coming off one of their best performances of the season, when the pass rush finally woke up and bullied a terrible team in the New York Jets. At the end of the day, I would expect the Chiefs offense to continue rolling while they ramp up new acquisition wide receiver Josh Downs. Chiefs 31, Atlanta 17 Nate Christensen Atlanta has been a surprisingly competitive team since quarterback Michael Penix Jr. came back. The Falcons have one of the dynamic duos of weapons in running back Bijan Robinson and Drake London. That alongside a decent offensive line has given the Falcons a shot to win any game. Their defense has been surprisingly competent, but after trading Jessie Bates, that will probably fall off. I expect Atlanta to have some nice drives against the Chiefs, but the game will play out similarly to the Jets game. At some point, the Chiefs pressure will get to a pocket-bound Penix and Atlanta won't be able to catch up offensively. Chiefs pull away in the second half. Chiefs 28, Falcons 17 Ron Kopp Jr. ( @RonOnChiefs ) If the Falcons hadn't traded away two starters this week, this would feel much more like a spot where the Chiefs could slip up. Still, noon kickoffs have seemed to come with slow starts for Kansas City this year, and this Falcons team still has a reason to fight to stay tied for first place in the NFC South. However, Atlanta has had more letdowns than triumphs this year, including a couple of weeks ago when the Tampa Bay Buccaneers ran for 342 yards as a team and didn't need a pass to win. This game should be a comfortable win for Kansas City because of its offense, leaning on the ground game once again to stay in rhtyhm and open up the middle of the field for passes. 2026 Standings Nate Chrstensen Maurice Elston Dakota Watson All nine panelists predicted the Chiefs to win by more than ten points. Ron (38-20) and Matt (28-13) had the most accurate Week 9 predictions with only 16 total points of error. Our readers were less optimistic about how Kansas City would perform. For example, a prediction calls for a 17-10 Chiefs win. They end up winning 16-10, so there were two points of error: the point spread was off by one point, the Kansas City score missed by one point, and the opponent's score was predicted correctly. But if the Chiefs lose the game 17-10, there were 28 points of error in the prediction: the point spread was off by 14 (the difference between +7 and -7), and both scores were off by 7.

Currently sitting at 3-5, the Texans must get back to their winning ways long-term if they plan on making a postseason push in the AFC. Right now, no one should be talking about the playoffs, especially since Houston has blown three fourth-quarter leads and remains winless at home. The good news? Sunday's matchup is on the road, a place where Houston is 3-1. The Texans will travel to Cleveland for a date with Deshaun Watson and the Browns in Week 10. Cleveland, which could be gunning for a wild-card berth under first-year coach Todd Monken, fell short on Sunday in a battle down in the bayou amid an overtime loss to the New Orleans Saints . Cleveland plans to start Watson, Houston's former franchise quarterback, but second-year passer Shedeur Sanders proved his potential by keeping the Browns alive in the Superdome. While throwing for nearly 200 yards and two touchdowns, Sanders was also sacked five times. Meanwhile, Cleveland's defense recorded five sacks, headlined by former Defensive Rookie of the Year Carson Schwesinger. "They're really good players, they're athletic and they're disruptive," Texans offensive coordinator Nick Caley said. "They've got that speed off the ball. They use their hands and they play really hard continuously. They're a handful for sure." As for Houston, quarterback C.J. Stroud threw for a season-high 384 yards and tied his career high in touchdown passes with five as Houston rolled past the Bolts in a 44-22 victory at SoFi Stadium. Despite a slow offensive start, Houston found a rhythm in the second quarter and never looked back. The Texans could be dealing with a multitude of injuries following Friday's practice. For the third straight day, rookie offensive lineman Keylan Rutledge did not practice. Running back Woody Marks and defensive ends Will Anderson Jr. and Danielle Hunter also could be in trouble after missing practice on Thursday and Friday. How do the experts feel about Sunday's showdown between a pair of AFC dark horses desperate to pick up a win for different reasons? picks.blurb: Texans vs. Browns: Final Score Predictions by Experts for Week 10 - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 10 NFL updates Maye, Hutchinson injured College football winners/losers Week 10 Fantasy Football Toolkit: Start/sit advice, rankings, sleepers, more UFC 334 takeaways Texans vs. Browns: Final Score Predictions by Experts for Week 10 Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Houston Texans enter Sunday's road game against the Cleveland Browns as 4.5-point favorites. The Browns have a better 5-4 record and a strong home defense, but their offensive struggles and Deshaun Watson's vulnerability under pressure have influenced many experts to favor Houston. The Texans have attracted support because of their explosive passing game and league-leading pass rush. But not every expert expects Houston to cover the spread. Some believe the Browns can use their home advantage and defensive pressure to keep Stroud from taking control. The predictions therefore point toward Houston as the more popular winner, but not necessarily an easy afternoon for the visitors. Picks: Texans 3 Browns 0 "Deshaun Watson should be back in the lineup, but the receiver matchup against Houston is favorable, with the Texans allowing the second-most fantasy points per game to WRs. Both rookies are worth considering as flex options," Eric Moody says. Houston has a 76.1% chance to win as per ESPN , while Daniel Oyefusi believes the Browns defense will have a bad time against C.J. Stroud and company. "The Texans are 9-3 ATS against the Browns since 2005. Cleveland's protection problems give Houston another opening. The Browns allow sacks at the league's highest rate, while Houston has the second-highest sack rate," Pamela Maldonado wrote. Picks: Texans 5, Browns 0 Brooke Cersosimo points out the Texans averaging 8.2 yards per passing play in 257 snaps Nico Collins has played. This is more than the San Francisco 49ers' league-leading 7.9. "Even sitting at 3-5, the Texans appear to be full steam ahead toward a playoff berth with the way their offense is playing and defense is improving. C.J. Stroud has Nick Caley's unit absolutely humming now that most of his main targets are healthy….Getting Deshaun Watson back is a boost for Cleveland, but even with him, the Browns have struggled to put together a full game, instead relying on a few big plays each week from their young stars. An all-around performance is exactly what the Browns must have to beat the current version of DeMeco Ryans' team," Cersosimo says. Bleacher Report Picks: Texans 6, Browns 1 Only Bleacher Report's Ian Hanford believes Cleveland can actually get past the Texans on Sunday. "The Texans probably see this as a revenge game as much as Watson does, but I think the Browns are able to muddy this one up for C.J. Stroud just enough to stay in the game, like we've seen them do multiple times this season," Hanford says of the Browns. Meanwhile, Brent Sobleski has a contrasting view. "It doesn't matter which quarterback is starting for the Browns, because the Texans defense should make their life miserable, even if that unit has been somewhat of a disappointment this season," Sobleski writes. Dawgs By Nature Picks: Texans 3, Browns 3 The balanced picks come as analyst Chris Pokorny believes C.J. Stroud's elite passing form collides directly with Cleveland's biggest strength, a disciplined, reliable pass defense. Dawgs By Nature's Thomas Moore picked the Browns but is still frustrated with Cleveland's erratic form since they lost winnable games against the New York Jets and New Orleans Saints. Moore knows how good the 3-5 Texans are but 2 of their 3 victories came against the Tennessee Titans and Los Angeles Chargers. Barry Shuck, who picked Houston, says, "Before the season began, I believed that the Texans would be one of the four best teams in the AFC. The Texans have a prolific passing attack and the Browns are ranked #13 against the pass, so that will be a good chess match. They can't run the ball, but neither can the Browns. Cleveland is middle of the pack in their passing game while Houston is listed in the lower third defending the pass. So, maybe the Browns can air it out to Harold Fannin and either of their two rookie receivers." The Arizona Republic "The Browns are 3-0 at home this season, but in the midst of a two-game losing skid. Cleveland won't be able to keep up with C.J. Stroud and the Texans, even if this game is at home," Jeremy Cluff says. Cluff's predicted scoreline: Texans 23, Browns 14 What Do These Predictions Mean? Houston Texans quarterback C.J. Stroud gestures during the first half against the Jacksonville Jaguars at Wembley Stadium.Kirby Lee - Imagn Images Houston enters as a 4.5-point favorite (-4.5), while Cleveland is a 4.5-point underdog (+4.5). This means Houston must win by at least five points to cover the spread. Historically, the Texans and Browns are tied at 7-7 in their regular-season series. However, Houston secured a 45-14 victory over Cleveland in their Wild Card round matchup on January 13, 2024. Houston will be looking to continue its success against Cleveland in Week 10. home.headline: Texans' brutal injury report just gave the Browns a golden opportunity
home.blurb: The Browns will host a banged-up Texans team that has already ruled out edge rusher Danielle Hunter, linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, wide receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., and left guard Keylan Rutledge. Will Anderson, Houston’s superstar pass rusher, also left Thursday’s practice with an ankle injury, was a nonparticipant on Friday, and is listed as questionable along with starting right tackle Trent Brown (wrist). Cleveland, meanwhile, has no major injury concerns. Top wide receiver Denzel Boston was listed as questionable with a toe injury , but the rookie practiced on Friday and is trending toward playing. The only Browns starter ruled out for Sunday is safety Ronnie Hickman with a concussion, but the Browns are deep at that position; second-round rookie Emmanuel McNeil-Warren is slated to start Sunday’s game alongside veteran Grant Delpit. There could be openings in the middle of the field for head coach Todd Monken to exploit with tight end Harold Fannin Jr. and shifty wideout KC Concepcion. To'oTo'o is a solid linebacker for the Texans, but he’s been in and out of the lineup due to injuries himself this season and has struggled in pass coverage. Texans' brutal injury report just gave the Browns a golden opportunity Skip to main content News The Cleveland Browns are one of six NFL teams with an undefeated record in home games entering Week 10, and their chances of extending that streak just got better based on Friday’s injury report . The Browns felt like legitimate 4.5-point home underdogs for this game, especially after Houston demolished the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 9. But if Anderson joins the Texans’ inactives list on Sunday, the Browns could find themselves in prime position to pull off another upset. Texans could be missing exactly what they needed to exploit the Browns' biggest weakness The Texans were shaping up to be an extremely tough matchup for Cleveland, and they probably still are. But their defense potentially being down its top two pass rushers, along with Al-Shaair on the second level, changes everything. Anderson enters Week 10 as the NFL leader in sacks with 9.5. As a team, Houston moved into a tie for first place with the Minnesota Vikings last week. No quarterback, meanwhile, has been sacked more than Deshaun Watson, who’s been taken down 33 times in eight games. Keeping Watson upright will be one of the keys to this game regardless of who’s rushing off the edges. The Texans are one of the few teams in the NFL who have a worse rushing attack than the Browns — Houston is 29th, Cleveland is 25th — and it would behoove the Browns to play this game from ahead and force quarterback C.J. Stroud to throw from the pocket against Denzel Ward and their elite secondary. Al-Shaair’s absence is also pivotal. Without him, the Texans could have to move Henry To'oTo'o to middle linebacker or lean on a part-time player like Wade Woodaz for Sunday's game. home.headline: Texans' Final Week 10 Injury Report vs. Browns Brings More Bad News
home.blurb: So there's a lot to take away from the Texans' injury report. Yet, the biggest and perhaps most surprising absence that Houston will be faced with this weekend surrounds their veteran star edge rusher Danielle Hunter, who's been ruled out after logging a limited practice on Thursday and didn't participate on Friday. As to how severe Hunter's injury is long-term, we don't really know yet. All we know is that Hunter likely suffered a hamstring injury during practice on Thursday, and it's serious enough to keep him out for one week–– and possibly more, knowing that the Texans are on a short week for Week 11. Azeez Al-Shaair is out for the Texans once again, seemingly with another groin injury that's kept him limited throughout the past several weeks . Another noteworthy name from the Texans' lineup who won't be playing on Sunday: their big trade acquisition of Marvin Harrison Jr. (hamstring), who was a limited participant in Wednesday's practice, but would not suit up for Thursday or Friday. And knowing that Harrison Jr. is dealing with a hamstring issue, there's a possibility that the Texans' wideout suffered that hamstring tweak in the middle of Houston's team session on Wednesday, and will now be forced out for a period of time. Montgomery's case is simple: he's been dealing with a groin injury dating back to Week 5 against the Tennessee Titans, has been out for the past three games, but was a full practice participant on Friday, that gives him hope to finally get back on the field for Week 10. However, for Anderson Jr., he deserves a bit more attention for his situation. He was a limited participant in practice on Thursday due to an ankle issue, and would inevitably not practice on Friday as a DNP. It’s a critical game for both teams. The Packers remain in last place in the NFC North, even while winning five of their last six games. The Vikings have lost two consecutive games following a 6-0 start. Who will win the game? And, with this being the halfway point of the season, who will lead the team in rushing, receiving and sacks? And, ultimately, what will be the team’s final record and playoff fate? Here are our Packers-Vikings picks and midseason predictions. Bill Huber’s Packers-Vikings Prediction The Vikings acquired Kirk Cousins this week. It’s a huge move for the Vikings, who somehow are 6-2 despite their quarterbacks’ inability to get the ball to Justin Jefferson. Cousins has faced the Packers 10 times while with the Vikings. He topped a 110 passer rating in seven of those games. OK, but what about this season? With the Raiders, Cousins ranked fifth in passing yards, second in touchdown passes and 11th in passer rating. Plain and simple, he remains a quality starting quarterback. Initially, I had the Vikings beat the Packers 20-17. I’m perhaps guilty of overvaluing Cousins based on his stats this season and his play against Green Bay over the years, but I think he’s good enough to make the Vikings a legit contender. He’s not good enough to carry an offense, though. On Friday, the Vikings ruled out tight end T.J. Hockenson and receiver Jauan Jennings. Helped by Cousins, Hockenson caught 86 passes in 2022 and 95 passes in 2023. On Sunday, the Vikings listed receiver Jordan Addison among their inactives due to a finger injury. At full strength, few quarterbacks could match Justin Jefferson, Addison and Hockenson for a Big Three. On Sunday, Cousins will be throwing to Jefferson, receiver Tai Felton (three catches) and tight end Gavin Bartholomew (seven catches). So, let’s flip-flop the original prediction. Packers 20, Vikings 17. Bill’s Record: 7-2. Jacob Westendorf’s Packers-Vikings Prediction Yes, Kirk Cousins is back, but Green Bay's defense is for real until proven otherwise. The Packers had some answers for Brian Flores' group in Week 1 until Jordan Love was snowed under by Minnesota's pressure. This time, Lambeau Field will be the X-factor as the offensive line will be able to hear Love manipulate the line of scrimmage, which will help him make one more play than Cousins, as the Packers score a big win heading into their bye week. Score: Packers 21, Vikings 17. Jacob’s Record: 6-3. Green Bay Packers quarterback Jordan Love (10) waits for the snap against the Dallas Cowboys at Lambeau Field. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? What Will Be Packers’ Final Record? Bill: 11-6 (Losses at home to the Vikings and Bills and at the Bears). Jacob: 12-5 (Losses at home against Buffalo and at Chicago). Where Will Packers Finish in NFC North? Bill: Last (with the same record as the Vikings but by losing the tiebreaker). Jacob: Second (Chicago wins the NFC North thanks to a win on Christmas Day at Soldier Field). Who Will Lead Packers in Sacks? Bill: Lukas Van Ness. I came up with this question in light of Micah Parsons’ presumptive return for the game against the Rams. Tucker Kraft has had a quiet season following last year’s torn ACL. It’s just part of coming off a major injury. So, while I thought about going with Parsons here, Van Ness will maintain the team lead and finish with eight sacks. Jacob: Lukas Van Ness. Van Ness has 4.5 sacks, which leads the team. His job should get a little easier with Micah Parsons' return to the lineup as he'll see less double teams. Parsons is a good bet here, as well, but has noted it may take him a while to look like himself again. The goal for the Packers is going to be to have him at his best in the postseason. Who Will Lead Packers in Rushing? Green Bay Packers running back Kaleb Johnson (26) rushes the ball against the New England Patriots at Gillette Stadium. | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Bill: Kaleb Johson leads the team with 172 rushing yards, just ahead of MarShawn Lloyd (149) and about double Josh Jacobs (80). Jacobs might only miss two games with his broken finger, meaning he’ll have five or six games to surge to the front. Jacob: Kaleb Johnson leads the team in rushing, which is incredible considering how his season has gone to date. The guess here is that he's out of Matt LaFleur's doghouse and going to be a more focal point of Green Bay's offense in Josh Jacobs' absence. That will continue even when Jacobs returns to the lineup. Who Will Lead Packers in Receiving Yards? Bill: Christian Watson has 879 receiving yards, putting him on pace to blow past 1,650 yards. Matthew Golden has 783 receiving yards, putting him on pace to push for 1,500 yards. I’ll take Golden to surge to the lead, though. He has five consecutive games of six-plus catches and four consecutive games with 10-plus targets. The sheer volume of passes going to Golden will push him past the explosive play off Watson, especially if last week’s game signals that his drops are behind him. The big question: Can they set the combined yardage record? Jacob: Christian Watson. This might be one of the most intriguing storylines down the stretch. Watson and Golden are neck and neck in this category now, with Watson holding a slight advantage. Watson is used to playing this late in the season and has made some big plays in big games. Golden has, as well, so this will be really close as the season comes to a close, but give us Watson to go over 1,200 yards for the season and earn the team's receiving title. Will Jordan Love Lead NFL in Passing Yards? Bill: Entering Sunday, Cincinnati’s Joe Burrow leads the NFL with 298.3 passing yards per game. Jordan Love is hot on his heels with a 290.9-yard average. That’s less than a first down per game. Playing five consecutive cold-weather games down the stretch isn’t going to help Love in his pursuit. Jacob: Yes, the only way the Packers can move the ball is on the right arm of Jordan Love. There's little reason to believe that's going to change, even when the elements start turning colder. Add in some games that could be potential shootouts, like a home game against Buffalo or a road game against Chicago. That could cause Love to pile up some big numbers. How Will the Season End? Bill: With the entire NFC North earning their way into the playoff field, the last-place Packers will squeak into the postseason as the No. 7 seed. It’s obviously a familiar place for the Packers. And it’s a death sentence. The No. 7 seed has to play at the No. 2 seed. If the No. 7 pulls off an upset, it will have to play at the No. 1 seed. So, let’s roll with the Packers upsetting the rival Bears in the wild-card round but meeting their maker against the playoff-rival 49ers in the divisional round. Jacob: The Packers will earn the NFC's fifth seed and have a date with the NFC South-winning Tampa Bay Buccaneers in the first round of the playoffs. A big game from Jordan Love and Christian Watson, coupled with a suffocating defensive performance in which Micah Parsons will collect three sacks and a forced fumble against Baker Mayfield, will give the team its first playoff win since 2023. They will follow that by avenging last year's loss in the playoffs to the Chicago Bears by knocking them out at Soldier Field in the divisional round on a game-winning field goal from Trey Smack. That sends them to San Francisco, a house of horrors, for the NFC Championship Game, where the season ultimately will end with Brock Purdy leading a late touchdown drive to send the Packers into an offseason short of the Super Bowl. No team has ever blitzed as much as this year's Vikings, and they have blitzed Packers QB Jordan Love with even greater frequency. picks.blurb: 3 Bold Vikings Predictions Heading Into Week 10 Showdown Against Packers Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI It seems like yesterday that the Vikings were hosting the Packers in Week 1 to kick off the 2026 season. Now, the two teams will conclude their regular-season series with a chilly match at Lambeau Field. Vikings fans are still riding the excitement from a major adrenaline injection early this week as the team reacquired quarterback Kirk Cousins via trade with the Las Vegas Raiders. What once looked like a potential beatdown in Green Bay now looks like a massive opportunity for the Vikings to end a two-game losing streak and sweep their biggest rival. There’s still a lot up in the air, especially since head coach Kevin O’Connell hasn't technically named Cousins the starter yet. But let’s be real: Cousins is starting unless there's a major setback . So, let’s dive into some predictions for Sunday, assuming “Kirko Chainz” makes his triumphant return. 1. Justin Jefferson returns to form (for real this time) Frick it, Justin Jefferson is down there somewhere. There is perhaps no larger beneficiary of the Cousins’ reunion tour than Jefferson. The seventh-year wide receiver is on pace to have the worst year of his career after poor QB play wrecked his 2025 campaign. Needless to say, it’s time for Jefferson to reclaim his spot on the wide receiver throne. Jefferson’s 98.9 receiving yards per game with Cousins far surpasses his 65 ypg average through six full games this season. Cousins’ mission on Sunday is simple: feed Jefferson. I’m predicting Jefferson will have a vintage performance with over 150 receiving yards and at least one touchdown. #Vikings QB Kirk Cousins says he saw Justin Jefferson today, and is excited to play with him again: “You don’t go chasing things, but you understand the player he is, and you go where your reads take you. You know he tends to make it right when you throw in his direction.” pic.twitter.com/zOoSnvilDO 2. Vikings defense holds the Packers to less than 20 points Green Bay’s 24 points per game ranks 12th-highest in the league through nine weeks, while Brian Flores and the Vikings defense are allowing a league-low 14.5 points per game to opposing offenses. Minnesota has held two of the league's best offenses, Detroit and Buffalo, to 19 and 23 points, respectively. This feat is even more impressive given the complete lack of help on the offensive side of the ball. “This roster has earned the right to explore the potential to maximize where we can take this thing.” -Vikings GM Nolan Teasley on the decision to trade for Kirk Cousins pic.twitter.com/TkkJVs0fsp 3. Minnesota gets back in the win column This one is pretty straightforward: I have the Vikings righting the ship against a talented Packers team and ending their slide down the NFC North standings. While many had assumed star pass rusher Micah Parsons would be back by now, the Vikings have the distinct advantage of avoiding him in both regular-season matchups. Two of these teams will miss the playoffs pic.twitter.com/7VewNM4oiT With a reenergized offense, a motivated Cousins returning to the scene of a career-altering injury, and O’Connell in “prove it” mode, I think we finally see a well-rounded 2026 Vikings squad in action. Published Nov 13, 2026 JASON HARMON Jason Harmon grew up a diehard Vikings fan and has been doing Vikings content and coverage since 2023. He is the Vikings Content Curator for Sleeper and is a host on Purple Daily’s in-season spinoff podcast “Before I Die”. Jason and his family moved to the Twin Cities from Arizona in 2025 as he started covering the team full time. My Vikings vs. Packers prediction and NFL picks say Kirk Cousins' emergency return to Minnesota won't be enough to survive an NFC North clash at Lambeau Field, where Tucker Kraft and Savion Williams are primed to power a Green Bay victory. "Cap'n Kirk is coming back!" was the immediate text sent to family when news broke that veteran quarterback Kirk Cousins was traded back to the Minnesota Vikings earlier this week. It was an emergency move to rescue a floundering offense wasting Brian Flores' dominant defense. Here are my expert NFL best bets ahead of Sunday's 1 p.m. ET kickoff on FOX. TOP PICK Vikings vs Packers prediction today: Packers moneyline The move to bring back Kirk Cousins is an upgrade for the Minnesota Vikings offense, but a half-cooked Cousins isn't going to be enough at Lambeau Field. Not with the tread wearing thin on this Minnesota defense. The Vikings' stop unit is playing on a short week after logging more than 42 minutes of work in Monday's loss to the Bills. Minnesota has spent an average of 36:41 on the field over the last three weeks , and the wear and tear is starting to show. Linebackers Blake Cashman (concussion) and Kyle Van Noy (calf) run the risk of missing Week 10. The Green Bay Packers are a long way removed from the team that lost to the Vikings in Week 1. Green Bay has been one of the best two-way teams since Week 6, ranking Top 10 in both EPA per play and EPA allowed in that span. There are some injury concerns for the Cheeseheads, which is why I'm going with the outright price and not laying -3.5. Vikings vs Packers combo The Cousins deal doesn't do much for me, and only offers better return on the Packers' moneyline at home. This Vikings stop unit is great, but it's possibly down some key guys and playing on a short week after logging major minutes on MNF. Tucker Kraft had a nice day against the Vikings in Week 1 and has been a red zone threat in recent weeks, with two TDs in his last three games. Savion Williams could be just what the Packers need to bust this Vikings defense. The burly slot receiver is a quick hitter who can pick up yards after the catch. His projections sit as high as 24+ yards in Week 10. Packers moneyline Tucker Kraft anytime touchdown Savion Williams 20+ receiving yards Vikings vs Packers touchdown scorer: Tucker Kraft The Packers have been able to strike for some home run touchdowns in recent weeks, but things shorten up against this Vikings defense. The Cheeseheads will have to work for six points when they enter the red zone. Kraft is a popular target, drawing nine passes inside the 20-yard line for seven receptions and three touchdowns. Kraft does his best work against zone coverage — which is something Brian Flores utilizes almost exclusively — and may catch a break if Cashman sits, as he's Minnesota's top coverage linebacker. Touchdown forecasts for Green Bay's TE range from 30% to 40% in Week 10. For more Week 10 touchdown angles, including Vikings receiver Justin Jefferson, see our NFL anytime touchdown picks for Week 10 . Vikings vs Packers player prop: Savion Williams 20+ receiving yards Second-year receiver Savion Williams is finding his way in this Packers offense after returning to action four games ago. Williams has stepped into the WR3 role, giving Love a big target in the slot. He's caught 11 of 13 targets for game outputs of five, 25, 32, and 47 yards. Both head coach Matt LaFleur and offensive coordinator Adam Stenavich gushed about Williams' skill set heading into Week 10, seeing the 6-foot-4, 222-pound receiver as a bigger part of the plan. "We're going to continue to try to find ways to get him the ball," LaFleur told the media. "You just see the power that he has." Given this Vikings defense's aggressive approach, Williams' role as a slot receiver becomes even more vital, with Love looking for a quick release from pressure. The Vikings have been exposed by slot options, most recently allowing the Bills' Khalil Shakir to pick up 58 yards on four receptions. Williams' Week 10 projections vary, sitting between 15 and 24.5 yards. My projection comes out to 21 yards receiving, but I see a higher ceiling, considering the matchup. Want more NFL player props? Yet, after losing back-to-back games, the Vikings know they can reach a higher ceiling, because they were in first place for the first seven weeks of the season. The hope is that trading for Kirk Cousins can resurrect Kevin O’Connell’s previously potent scoring attacks after ranking just 27th in points this season. Yet, considering the four-time Pro Bowl QB has already operated Kevin O’Connell’s offense for two seasons, it shouldn’t take the 38-year-old long to get back in the saddle. Even though he was just acquired Tuesday, Cousins understands the importance of the Vikings’ next matchup, against the division rival Green Bay Packers, who enter the week at 6-3, in fourth place of the division. As Sunday approaches, it’s time to dive into four bold predictions for this week’s Vikings-Packers game. One person who has to be thrilled with Cousins’ return is Justin Jefferson who has seen his targets dwindle since employee No. 8 left town. Yet, Jefferson already has chemistry with Cousins, and the new Vikings QB is playing at an elite level. It may be as easy as riding a bike with Jefferson reuniting with Cousins, which could lead to the best game No. 18 has had since Week 18 of the 2024 season, when he went off for 192 yards and a touchdown. The Vikings have gotten horrid QB play all season long. While Carson Wentz and Kyler Murray had stretches where they took care of the football, they also missed several open receivers. Cousins will be much better reading the field and finding the open man. As a result, we’ll see him become the first Vikings QB to have a 300-yard game all season. Now that he has a quarterback who will actually find him when he’s open, Jauan Jennings has a chance to have a breakout game with the Vikings. He hasn’t gone over 34 yards as a Viking yet, but that will change on Sunday as he ends up playing a big role in a Vikings’ victory, making key blocks and going off for a season-high 80 yards and a touchdown. Performances like this are why he joined the Vikings and wanted to stick around when trade opportunities presented themselves. The first time these two teams faced off, things got a bit wacky on both sides. Kyler Murray left the game with a concussion in the first quarter, and Jordan Love went nuclear in the first half before the Vikings put the clamps on him in the second half. picks.headline: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup
picks.blurb: Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Fantasy Football Week 10 NFL updates Maye, Hutchinson injured College football winners/losers Week 10 Fantasy Football Toolkit: Start/sit advice, rankings, sleepers, more UFC 334 takeaways Packers vs. Vikings Odds: Opening line for Week 10 matchup (Photo by Todd Rosenberg/Getty Images) | Getty Images Justis Mosqueda · SB Nation Mon, November 9, 2026 at 6:40 AM UTC · 2 min read Advertisement Advertisement About Our Ads College Sports Sports Business Women's Sports College & High School Adventure Sports What & How To Watch Responsible Gaming Share Your Feedback About Our Ads The Green Bay Packers (6-3) are set to be three-point favorites over the Minnesota Vikings (6-1) in Week 10, according to FanDuel's numbers . That number comes with a little juice at -120, and the Packers are -178 favorites, which comes with an implied probability of 64 percent. If you had said this a few weeks ago, when the Packers' offensive line was drowning, no one would have bought it. Now, after Green Bay finally had a 100-yard rushing performance and beat down on the New England Patriots in all three phases of the game, it looks like the Packers have a real opportunity to make a push for the postseason. The Vikings have played two fewer games than the Packers because: 1) they've already had their bye week and 2) they're playing on Monday Night Football against the Buffalo Bills. After that game, they'll have a short(er) week and have to travel on the road to Lambeau Field. Their starting quarterback, Kyler Murray, is currently dealing with a hamstring injury and will not play against the Bills. We'll have to see if it heals up by the time they kick off against the Packers, or if it'll be Carson Wentz — their current replacement starter — under center. The only other quarterback in Minnesota is Max Brosmer (53-man roster). Below is the current playoff picture in the NFC: San Francisco 49ers: 7-1 (NFC West) Minnesota Vikings: 6-1 (NFC North) New York Giants: 5-2-1 (NFC East) Carolina Panthers: 3-5 (NFC South) Chicago Bears: 7-2 Detroit Lions: 6-2 Green Bay Packers: 6-3 Seattle Seahawks: 5-4 Los Angeles Rams: 5-4 Dallas Cowboys: 4-5 New Orleans Saints: 3-5 Tampa Bay Buccaneers: 3-6 Atlanta Falcons: 3-6 Arizona Cardinals: 3-6 Washington Commanders: 2-5-1 Philadelphia Eagles: 2-7 The Packers are holding onto the seventh seed right now, where they've been for weeks, but the NFC North keeps winning — as do the Seattle Seahawks and Los Angeles Rams, the teams trying to hunt them down from behind. The NFC is so wonky, with the "good" teams being in the North and West, not the South and East, that the 3-6 Tampa Bay Buccaneers currently have about as good a chance of making the playoffs (by winning the NFC South) as do the Los Angeles Rams (a .500 team that is essentially locked into a playoff spot or nothing in 2026), per The Athletic's playoff simulator . In short, there are seven North and West teams fighting for five playoff spots in the NFC, and then there's whatever the hell is happening in the East and South. Do not be surprised at all if a sub-.500 NFC South team ends up hosting a 12-5 (or better record) NFC North team in the wild card round this year.

away.blurb: LP = Limited participant in practice. DNP = Did not participate in practice. Probable = the league defines a Probable injury designation as a 75% or greater chance of playing. Historically, 95% of players designated probable are active and played on game day. Questionable = the league defines a Questionable injury designation as being ‘uncertain’ of whether the player will play or not. This replaces the former definition of having a 50% chance of playing. Historically, 70-75% of players with a Questionable injury designation were active and played on game day. Doubtful = The league defines a Doubtful injury designation to mean the player is unlikely to participate in the game. In practical terms, teams use the designation when a player has less than a 50% chance to suit up, and active game appearances from this designation remain rare. Historically only around 6% of players with a Doubtful designation are active and played on game day. Out = will not play. Players with this designation are not active on game day and league rules prohibit them from playing. For the Vikings, no change in injury status for anybody compared to Wednesday’s estimates. That doesn’t bode well for any of the players that have yet to practice this week being available on Sunday. We’ll see if there are any upgrades tomorrow, but otherwise it looks like in addition to Blake Cashman, Hockenson, Ingram-Dawkins, Jennings, and Van Noy may not be available on Sunday.
