home.headline: Packers-Vikings Wednesday Injury Report: Huge List Filled With Big Names
home.blurb: Officially, the Packers did not practice on Wednesday as they get ready for Sunday’s showdown against the Minnesota Vikings. If they would have, five starters would not have practiced and a total of 16 players were dealing with one issue or another. Rhyan was injured during the opening series at Detroit. So, he missed most of that game and then the next two games. Coach Matt LaFleur said Rhyan could “potentially” return this week, but that he would not have practiced on Wednesday might not be a good sign for Sunday. The questions on the offensive line run deeper than center. Left guard Aaron Banks (knee/hip) would have been limited participation, a continuation of a season filled with injuries. He’s played only 137 snaps. Of his three starts, he was unable to go the distance against the Jets in Week 2 or the Patriots last week. When Banks was knocked out of the New England game, Kevin Zeitler made his Packers debut. Well, he would have been limited participation, as well, with an ankle injury. Linebacker Ty’Ron Hopper, who played only two defensive snaps vs. the Patriots due to a pregame chest injury, would have been limited due to illness; the chest is not mentioned on the injury report. Kicker Trey Smack (right calf) and receiver Savion Williams (groin) were listed as limited participation, as well. Skyy Moore Designated for Return Receiver Skyy Moore was designated for return after missing the last four games with an ankle injury. He is averaging 16.0 yards per punt return, highlighted by a 63-yarder against the Jets, and 27.5 yards per kickoff return. Both figures lead the team. Running back Chris Brooks (ankle) and edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), who are entering their second week of practice after being designated for return, would have been limited. Brooks would be a big addition against the Vikings’ blitzing defense. Limited participation: LG Aaron Banks (knee/hip), RB Chris Brooks (ankle), G/T Travis Glover (knee), LB Ty’Ron Hopper (illness), WR Skyy Moore (ankle), edge Micah Parsons (knee/illness), K Trey Smack (right calf), WR Savion Williams (groin), G Kevin Zeitler (ankle). Note: Brooks, Moore and Parsons have been designated to return and are within their 21-day practice window. Limited participation: S Jay Ward (knee), QB Carson Wentz (ankle). picks.blurb: Jaguars-Titans Week 10 National Predictions Roundup: Why Jacksonville Can't Overlook Tennessee Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- The Jacksonville Jaguars have an important AFC South battle in Week 10, with a chance to keep their momentum rolling as they battle for seeding in the AFC. But the Jaguars can't afford to focus on anything about seeding, the AFC, or their new pieces when 1 p.m. comes along. The Jaguars are set to battle a Tennessee Titans team that has played its best football of the season over the last three weeks, losing two one-score games against teams with winning records and earning their first win of the season in Week 6 on the road against the Indianapolis Colts. The Jaguars, sitting at 6-2 after back-to-back post-bye week wins, will need a road win in Nashville to keep their own momentum. That momentum got a jolt over the week with trade deadline additions of Jordan Davis, Jessie Bates III, and Davon Godchaux, but the Jaguars believe they have kept their eyes on the ball during their preparation for the week. “I think sometimes when you maybe make a player acquisition like this, and you get some star power, you get some big names and things like that, I think maybe there's a – I've seen in the past some teams that, like almost kind of, ‘Oh, okay, we're good now. And those guys will make the play.’ And I don't think that's how our building operated at all when that news broke," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said this week. "It was almost just like, ‘Alright, we know we're a good team. We know we're a good team and these players are only here to help us take it to the next level.’ But we're not going to sit back and say, ‘Okay, well, Jessie Bates will make the play or Jordan Davis and Davon, they'll make the play. We don't have to go and do it.’ I think our guys have a lot of pride in the way that they prepare, the way that they practice." How do the national predictions see this one playing out, however? We take a look below. Sports Illustrated Albert Breer: Jaguars Eva Geitheim: Jaguars Mitch Goldich: Jaguars Mike Kadlick: Jaguars Gilbert Manzano: Jaguars Conor Orr: Jaguars John Pluym: Jauars Matt Verderame: Jaguars Matt Bowen: Jaguars Mike Clay: Jaguars Jeremy Fowler: Jaguars Dan Graziano: Jaguars Kalyn Kahler: Jaguars Pamela Maldonado: Jaguars Eric Moody: Jaguars Jason Reid: Jaguars Ben Solak: Jaguars Lindsey Thiry: Jaguars Seth Wickersham: Titans Jeremy Bergman: Jaguars Brooke Cersosimo: Jaguars Gennaro Filice: Jaguars Bobby Kownack: Jaguars Dan Parr: Jaguars Joe Buscaglia: Jaguars Jon Greenberg: Jaguars Larry Holder: Jaguars Nick Kosmider: Jaguars Josh Kendal: Jaguars Austin Mock: Jaguars Jacksonville Jaguars On SI Analysis The Jaguars do not get the sweep here, earning 29 of 30 votes. Still, that is quite an easy summary of what people expect to happen in this one. The Jaguars are one of the AFC's best teams and have been the most-talked-about team of the trade deadline week after their all-in moves, though two of the three defenders they traded for will not appear against the Titans. Even without Jordan Davis and Jessie Bates III on hand , the Jaguars will have a high standard on defense. The Jaguars do not like how many rushing yards they allowed to the Baltimore Ravens last week, just like they didn't like the fact that they didn't complete the shutout against the Indianapolis Colts in Week 8. With that in mind, they are facing a Titans team that has played much better offensively as of late. The Titans offense has flirted with being ranked in the top-half of teams in terms of both offensive EPA/Play and Success Rate after their big scoring outputs against the Cleveland Browns and Cincinnati Bengals. Cam Ward is playing better after early-season struggles, and Tony Pollard has been amongst the NFL's most productive runners over the last few weeks. This isn't the hapless Titans offense from the start of the year, even without Carnell Tate. But the Jaguars' defense simply feels like it has been hitting on all cylinders. The only quarterbacks to really have success against them this season in terms of moving the ball have been CJ Stroud and Joe Burrow, and Ward is not that. The Jaguars can't afford to treat the Titans like the Ravens a week ago, but this should still be a game that they control. On the other side of the ball, the Titans have lost their two best defenders in Jeffery Simmons and Amani Hooker due to trades, and the numbers have reflected it. It does not feel like their secondary should be able to keep up with the Jaguars, and I am going Jacksonville 34, Titans 12 in this one. picks.blurb: 5 Bold Predictions for Jaguars vs. Titans: Which New Addition Makes the First Big Play Skip to main content SI.COM Betting Sites Sportsbook Promos BetMGM Bonus Code Fanatics Sportsbook Promo Canada Sportsbook Promos bet365 CA Bonus Code Rainbet Promo Code Stake Promo Code PREDICTION MARKETS College Market Prediction Market Apps Prediction Market Promos Kalshi Promo Code Kalshi Referral Code Apps like Kalshi Polymarket Promo Code Polymarket Referral Code Novig Promo Code Underdog Promo Code Stadium Wonders Digital Covers Push Notifications Digital Subscription Customer Service Prospects by SI JACKSONVILLE, Fla. -- After a frantic start to the week that saw the Jacksonville Jaguars make the biggest moves of this year's NFL Trade Deadline, it is worth remember that the Jaguars do, in fact, have an opponent on Sunday. The 6-2 Jaguars are set to travel to Nissan Stadium to face the Tennessee Titans in Week 10, their first game since making blockbuster trades for Jessie Bates and Jordan Davis, along with adding Davon Godchaux for a sixth-round pick. For a Jaguars team that has their eyes set on an AFC South title and a top seed in the playoffs, they are treating the Titans with the same seriousness that they treated the Indianapolis Colts and Baltimore Ravens over the last two weeks. So, how do we see the Jaguars' Week 10 battle with the Titans playing out? We break it down below. Jessie Bates Records An Interception While it certainly remains to be seen if the Jaguars will actually play any of their new defensive pieces against the Titans, I believe they will. Jakobi Meyers and Greg Newsome each played in their first games with the franchise last season after joining the team during that same week, and I think that means we see the trio make their Jaguars debuts. In the process, I think we see Bates create his first Jaguars takeaway right off the bat. Cam Ward is far from the most turnover-prone quarterback the Jaguars have played this season; that distinction goes to Daniel Jones. But he is right near the league average in interception rate, and he has made some egregious decisions with the ball over his last two seasons as a starter. This feels like the perfect week for Anthony Campanile to cook some pressure looks up to confuse Ward, and Bates is a natural playmaker. I think we see his impact right away. Parker Washington Catches 2 TDs The Titans' defense has been ... not very good against slot receivers this season. The Titans rank in the bottom-5 in the NFL against slot targets in each of the following categories: yards per play allowed, yards after the catch allowed, yards after the catch over expectation, and average seperation. The Titans have simply been a mess in the slot, even moving long-time outside cornerback Alontae Taylor to the slot despite signing him in March to play on the outside. As a result, I think this is a Parker Washington week. He is the clear No. 1 receiver in the offense, and I think he shakes off some inconsistent moments we have seen as of late and has a huge game against the Titans. Washington is due for a big performance, and I think we see it this Sunday against the Titans. Cam Ward Throws For Fewer Than 150 Yards There have been 275 quarterback performances this season. In just 39 of those performances, we have seen quarterbacks throw for fewer than 150 yards. Cam Ward makes up two of those games, a number that is trumped only by Bo Nix and Malis Willis which is, well, not great company to be in as far as productive gunslingers go. Ward has been more productive and explosive as of late and is coming off one of the best games of his career, but I predict the Jaguars limit Ward to under 150. Ward threw for just 141 yards against the Jaguars in Week 13 a year ago, and the Jaguars limited Daniel Jones and Joe Fagnano to a combined 189 yards over the last eight quarters. The Jaguars' pass defense is clicking, largely due to the work of defensive coordinator Anthony Campanile, and I believe we see it continue this week. Jaguars Limit Tony Pollard to Under 4.0 YPC Titans running back Tony Pollard has been on a tear over the last few weeks. Pollard, who has rushed for 246 yards and five touchdowns over the last two games, broke out of a mid-season skid and has been able to average over 4.0 yards per carry in every single game but two this season. While Pollard has been one of the NFL's more impressive runners over the last few weeks, I expect the Jaguars to be ready to bottle him up on Sunday. Again, I think the Jaguars will play Davis and Godchaux on Sunday. But even if they don't, I do not think the Titans have the offense to keep the Jaguars off-balance enough to run the ball on them. Teams can only run the ball on the Jaguars when the Jaguars are threatened by the early-down pass, and I do not see the Titans having much success there. Walker Little Pitches Another Shutout The Jaguars have seen Walker Little play really, really well over the last few weeks since stepping into the lineup for an injured Anton Harrison. According to NextGenStats, Little has allowed pressure on just 6.4% of his pass blocks, the fifth lowest rate in the league among left tackles (minimum 100 pass blocks). On his 109 pass blocks, his 87.2% 1-on-1 matchup rate is the highest in the league among left tackles; his 6.3% 1-on-1 pressure rate allowed is the third lowest pressure rate allowed in the league. “The experience always helps. Confidence is a heck of a thing, and I think he's the one that said it in an interview that humility helped. Where obviously he became our swing tackle, and all that guy has done is just stay the course," Jaguars head coach Liam Coen said on Wednesday. "Like, never got up, too down. He's just very steady. I really like Walker's play demeanor, the look in his eye recently and not taking everything so seriously. He's able to have fun with it. He's out there playing a game that he loves and competes with, but he's playing at a high level right now. He's got confidence, and you can tell.” Little will mostly draw Titans pass-rusher Jacob Martin, who has had a good year. But after strong showings against the Houston Texans' pass-rush duo in London a month ago and then a dominant outing against Trey Hendrickson last week , I think Little has the edge entering Week 10. He is playing some of the best football of his career right now, and I predict it leads to another shutout. Fans wouldn't be blamed for forgetting that we've got football this coming Sunday after days on end filled with rumors and breaking news at the end of every sentence. Not only do the Titans play in Week 10, but they're hosting AFC South-rivals. The Jacksonville Jaguars, one of the most active buyers at the trade deadline, are coming to Nashville to boast their new pickups. The last time Tennessee faced Jacksonville, the Titans lost 41-7 at the very end of the 2025 season. Cam Ward missed the majority of that game after exiting early with a shoulder injury, and his healthy showing tomorrow is the key to a potential Titans upset. Will: Cam Ward stays hot in Carnell Tate's return Ward nearly led Tennessee to a victory over the (now) 6-2 Cincinnati Bengals in Week 8. The Titans falling short 36-43 in overtime was partly due to Ward taking a costly sack late in regulation, but the QB can't at all be blamed for losing a game he kept Tennessee in. With WR1 Carnell Tate trending toward a return, Ward should have all of his weapons in place to put up another promising game. The Titans even kept RB Tony Pollard at the deadline for Ward's own sake. Again, Jacksonville bulked up at the deadline - their defense specifically - but Tennessee leaving the offense untouched said loud and clear that this franchise believes in Ward. With a newly-gutted defense, the Titans will be relying on Ward to try and secure the win. Won't: Jaguars' overhauled defense clicks immediately Directly opposing Ward is that new-look Jags defense. In addition to adding All-Pro S Jessie Bates III, Jacksonville also acquired defensive tackles Jordan Davis and Davon Godchaux. If Tennessee falls short (as is likely expected), it will be because the Jaguars' defense put a stopper in Ward and the offense's growth. That could be one reason among many, but it seems to be the most relevant by far regarding this specific matchup. Prediction: Titans lose, 34-23 At the end of the day on Sunday, I expect Jacksonville will overwhelm Tennessee. I don't believe it will be in blowout fashion, and this is primarily because of the stable flashes of progress Ward showed in Week 8. But between their overhauled defense and Trevor Lawrence manning things under center on offense, the Titans are truly facing a championship contender this week. Perhaps the home field will help blunt the blow, as well as the team debuting their Music City jerseys. I love the jerseys. I like what we saw from Cam Ward in his most recent game. But this Jaguars team has the AFC South in a headlock, and the 1-7 Titans simply don't have enough on paper to climb out of a double-digit projected loss in this one. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. (Video via Jake Arthur/ColtsRoundtable) Under the current circumstances, it by no means makes sense to favor the Indianapolis Colts (2-7) in a game. They were already reeling enough to fire general manager Chris Ballard last month, then trade franchise pillars Quenton Nelson and DeForest Buckner the following week. Then this week, the fire sale continued as the team traded its top two active receivers, Josh Downs and Keenan Allen. However, despite the clear focus on the Colts' future rather than the present, this week's opponent, the Miami Dolphins (1-7), is in even worse shape. Three of their best players are unavailable this week, as quarterback Malik Willis and defensive tackle Zach Sieler were placed on Injured Reserve, and center Aaron Brewer is out with a concussion. Kyle McCord will be making his first-career start against a defensive coordinator in Lou Anarumo, who enjoys making things as difficult as possible for inexperienced quarterbacks. The Colts are 3.5-point favorites in this one, according to FanDuel Sportsbook , but what do the local experts think? Here is how the ColtsRoundtable staff sees Sunday's game unfolding. Jake Arthur ( @JakeArthurNFL ): Colts 24, Dolphins 10 "I'm going to give head coach Shane Steichen the benefit of the doubt and say that he uses this time as an opportunity to reimagine what the offense does. Right now, all you have is two solid runners and a bunch of pedestrian receivers whose career calling cards are centered around chunk plays. Daniel Jones is going to have to sacrifice the short-throw safety of guys like Downs and Allen and push the ball a little further to the likes of Laquon Treadwell, Ashton Dulin, and Deion Burks. "On the defensive side of the ball, the young players are actually providing something promising to watch. The defense overall isn't great, but young linemen such as Adetomiwa Adebawore, Jaylahn Tuimoloau, and Caden Curry are playing really well as of late, and rookie linebacker CJ Allen continues to improve. I think Anarumo thrives against young, inexperienced quarterbacks like McCord. Dial up the pressure." Jake on the season: 5-4 Zach Hicks ( @ZachHicks2 ): Colts 16, Dolphins 13 "This week's game between the Colts and the Dolphins has the makings of a slugfest. The Colts come into this one riding a five-game losing streak while having Treadwell as the only receiver on the roster with more than 100 snaps played this season. "Meanwhile, the Dolphins are giving McCord his first-ever start at quarterback with Willis on Injured Reserve. Points will be at a premium in this one, so I expect a low-scoring affair. The Colts narrowly get the win in my prediction but we should be in store for some ugly football this Sunday." Zach on the season: 7-2 The Colts take on the Dolphins at Lucas Oil Stadium in Indianapolis on Sunday at 1:00 p.m. ET on CBS .

away.headline: Dolphins-Colts Game Preview and Predictions: Can Miami Overcome Injuries?
away.blurb: That season-opening win was part of a fantastic start for the Colts, who once were 8-2 and very much looking like legit AFC contenders. The bottom then fell out and it hasn't stopped falling out, Indianapolis losing 14 of its past 16 games going back to last November 23. From this end, it's just difficult to give the Dolphins the nod here with an unproven quarterback who will have to work with the same subpar supporting cast that's hampered Willis so far this season, and without Aaron Brewer out on top of everyhing. Analysis: This is the dog game of the week between two struggling teams. But one is young and playing hard on the way up, while one is on the way down after trading away assets. The problem for Miami is that quarterback Malik Willis is out. That means Kyle McCord will start at quarterback. Miami will hang around against the depleted Colts team, but the Colts will win it late. For a change, the Miami Dolphins are given a chance by more than just one or two national media members heading into their Week 10 game against the Indianapolis Colts — and that's despite the injury to starting quarterback Malik Willis. The Dolphins will go into the game with a 1-7 record but after giving playoff contenders New England and Detroit a battle before losing at Hard Rock Stadium the past two weeks. That, of course, with quarterback Malik Willis and standout defensive lineman Zach Sieler in the lineup, with both now on injured reserve. The Colts also have their issues, having traded four veterans — Quenton Nelson, DeForrest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs — in the midst of a wildly disappointing season that's already seen GM Chris Ballard lose his job. The Colts did retain star running back Jonathan Taylor and veteran defensive tackle Grove Stewart, who had been rumored to be on the move, and it's not like they're playing for draft position since their 2027 first-round pick belongs to the New York Jets as the result of the Sauce Gardner trade that keeps looking worse every day. Indianapolis is favored by 3.5 points, according to the Fan Duel Sportsbook . This is the second consecutive year the teams will face each other, the 2025 meeting coming in the season opener when the Colts humbled the Dolphins, 33-8, in a game that set the stage for Miami's disappointing 7-10 season that produced the regime change and rebuilding project that's going on right now. This is why the Dolphins are being given a chance — even predicted by some — to win the game Sunday despite having a quarterback on his third team in two years ready to play his first real NFL snaps. The Colts gave Dallas all it could handle last week before losing in overtime, and they may benefit from the uncertainty of their roster being done now that the NFL trade deadline has passed. The Dolphins defense probably will be able to keep the score close, but we'd still call it something like 20-10 for the Colts. Jarrett Bell: Colts 26, Dolphins 20 Nick Brinkerhoff: Dolphins 13, Colts 10 Chris Bumb

away.headline: Miami Dolphins QB Malik Willis to injured reserve
away.blurb: After he was aquired, McCord said of his strengths: "Knowing the call and then seeing what the defense plays and getting the ball to the right guy on time, allowing the playmakers to go out and make plays. And then my accuracy too, I think those two things really showed in the preseason and are probably a big reason why I'm here." Kyle McCord, acquired in a preseason trade, is expected to start in Willis's absence. Willis has struggled this season, and his performance has not secured his position as the team's long-term quarterback. The Dolphins, currently 1-7, may consider selecting a quarterback with a potential top pick in the upcoming NFL Draft. MIAMI GARDENS ― Miami Dolphins quarterback Malik Willis is headed to injured reserve and will miss at least four games, a league source confirmed on Tuesday, Nov. 10. Willis has played through injuries to a groin, a toe and a thumb. This is a core issue, according to reports. Willis will miss games at Indianapolis, at Buffalo, vs. the Jets and at Denver. Kyle McCord , whom Miami acquired in a trade from Packers before the season, is in line to start. Willis' ranks in the NFL are: 27th (passer rating), 26th (passing yards) and 25th (passing touchdowns). Despite some glimpses, Willis has not yet provided assurances that he is Miami's quarterback of the future. With a Top 3 NFL Draft pick on the horizon in April of 2027, quarterback will certainly be an option. Willis has a big arm and athleticism, when healthy. But he continues to work on decision-making, accuracy and timing. Willis, 27, agreed to a 3-year, $67 million contract with $45 million guaranteed. Miami would like Willis to at least be their starting quarterback for two seasons. But nothing in life is guaranteed, especially for NFL quarterbacks. McCord, 24, played at Ohio State and Syracuse and was a 6th round pick of the Eagles. On trading deadline day, the Dolphins did not make a deal. So Austin Jackson, Josh Uche and anyone else mentioned as intriguing trade candidates remain on the roster. Joe Schad is a journalist covering the Miami Dolphins and the NFL at The Palm Beach Post . Hafley said Bell got hit in the leg during practice and it did not have to do with his prior knee injury. Hafley said he expects Chop Robinson and Josh Uche to step up in defensive lineman Zach Sieler's absence . Sieler is out for the season after season-ending biceps surgery. This article originally appeared on Palm Beach Post: Dolphins injury report: QB Malik Willis, C Aaron Brewer out vs. Colts Miami Dolphins All-Pro center Aaron Brewer remains in concussion protocol and will not play against the Indianapolis Colts on Sunday. Coach Jeff Hafley said Andrew Meyer will start in Brewer's place. Meyer, who started a game last season, has worked closely with Kyle McCord since the quarterback's arrival from Green Bay. McCord will be making his first NFL start in place of Malik Willis, who is on injured reserve. "He's done a nice job. Have a lot of confidence in Meyer," Hafley said. Hafley also said his new quarterback has a "very calm confidence" about him. "He's got a quiet leadership about him. He's got a confidence to him. He's very calm in the huddle. And he seems to be grasping everything really well," Hafley said. "I think he's done a really good job in the two practices that we've had. (Friday's) a big day again, getting more in the red zone and polishing up some stuff. "But again, this will be a process, right? I'm not going to expect him to look perfect. There's going to be hopefully some really good moments for him and then there's going to be some that we're going to have to continue to grow in these next games. But I'm excited for him and I appreciate how he's worked, attacked the game plan and how he's kind of communicating and developing chemistry with the players around him in the huddle." "The way Chop's playing and really practicing, I think he's a great example of what it's supposed to look like," Hafley said. "And I think he's going to grow into one of those roles."

away.headline: Colts get good news at defensive end; see all the roster moves the Colts made for Dolphins game
away.blurb: On Saturday, the Colts announced that starting edge rusher Arden Key , who suffered a hamstring injury in the team's Week 4 win in London against the Commanders and missed five games, had been activated off IR and will make his return Sunday. Key was a full participant in the Colts' three practice this week after having his 21-day window to return to the active roster opened earlier in the week. In his place, the Colts put two more injured players – starting linebacker Akeem Davis-Gaither and veteran tight end Mo Alie-Cox – on IR. Davis-Gaither aggravated a lingering knee injury during the Colts' Week 8 loss to the Jaguars and missed all three practices the following week, as well as the team's Week 9 game against the Cowboys. The veteran linebacker also did not see the field this week. Alie-Cox suffered a groin injury during last Sunday's home game against Dallas and did not practice this week. Both players will be eligible to return following four missed games – which, with the Colts' Week 13 bye, won't be until Indianapolis' Week 14 away game Dec. 13 at the Eagles . The Colts will be additionally short-handed at tight end Sunday, as they announced Will Mallory, who was added to the injury report Friday with limited participation due to a hamstring injury, will be out for Sunday's game – the seventh player (including Davis-Gaither and Alie-Cox, who were later moved to IR) to be ruled out ahead of Week 10. The Colts will have starter Tyler Warren and rotational tight ends Drew Ogletree and Pharaoh Brown available. In order to bolster what was also an injury-laden linebacker unit, with Jaylon Carlies (neck) ruled out for Sunday's game on Friday along with Davis-Gaither, the Colts signed rookie former undrafted free agent West Weeks to the team's 53-man roster from the practice squad, setting up the potential for the LSU standout to make his NFL debut Sunday. Before Saturday, the Colts had also already ruled out starting right tackle Jalen Travis (knee) and rotational defensive tackle Jerry Tillery (calf). With Travis' absence, the Colts could shift starting right guard Matt Goncalves , who played tackle in college, to Travis' position on the line, and then backfill Goncalves' spot with backup guard Dalton Tucker – making, along with relatively new starting left guard Jalen Farmer, three starting offensive linemen in new positions compared to three weeks ago. Along with Watkins, the Colts had previously signed veteran practice squad wideout Nick Westbrook-Ikhine to the 53-man roster following the trades of starting receivers Josh Downs and Keenan Allen on Tuesday ahead of the NFL's trade deadline. Return specialist Anthony Gould will start in place of Downs, and Ashton Dulin , Deion Burks and Westbrook-Ikhine will see additional opportunities alongside continued starter Laquon Treadwell . With both teams looking to turn their seasons around, the Saints will need another strong performance from quarterback Tyler Shough and their defense to secure consecutive victories for the first time this season. Here are our Saints ON SI staff predictions for Sunday's matchup between New Orleans and Carolina. Grant Chachere, Lead Writer: L 21-14 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints wide receiver Chris Olave (12) makes a catch with Cleveland Browns cornerback Tyson Campbell (7) defending during the fourth quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. I think this will be a relatively close game for the Saints. While the defense is flawed in some areas, New Orleans arguably has the best pass rush duo in Chase Young and Carl Granderson , who are both in the top five in sacks. However, I’m still worried about its inability to stop the run, especially when the opposing team has a solid running back. Unfortunately for the Saints, Carolina has a pretty dadgum good running back in Chuba Hubbard , who has rushed for 619 yards and reached paydirt five times this season. On top of that, the Saints’ defense will go up against a better quarterback in Bryce Young , who has thrown for 2,197 yards with 18 touchdowns and six interceptions and is the face of the fourth-best passing attack in the NFL and one that features wide receiver Tetairoa McMillan (46 receptions, 625 yards, 3 touchdowns). The good thing for the Saints is that the Panthers aren’t the greatest defense when it comes to stopping the run as they are 28th in the league in rushing yards allowed. The Saints were able to run the ball effectively last week against the Cleveland Browns , who also had a similar issue, but execution will be key. Can the Saints pull off the win and remain in first place? It’s definitely a possibility. However, I cannot trust Kellen Moore’s ability to manage and put together a game plan for four quarters because Tyler Shough and the Saints have won three games despite the offensive staff’s ineptitude. Also, add on the fact that the Saints are missing two of their starting offensive linemen on an already porous offensive line in center Erik McCoy and right tackle Taliese Fuaga , the Saints’ chances of winning decrease. Prediction: Panthers 21, Saints 14 Doug Joubert, Publisher: W 27-21 Nov 8, 2026; New Orleans, Louisiana, USA; New Orleans Saints quarterback Tyler Shough (6) looks to pass against the Cleveland Browns during the third quarter at Caesars Superdome. Mandatory Credit: Stephen Lew-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places. I'm not quite sure what to think of this "new" Saints team. It's almost like there's a new set of faces each week in different places. Jordyn Tyson should be full speed for the first time this year. Trevor Etienne will be on the field, probably taking it easy at first, the way Tyson did when coming back from a hamstring injury. The offensive line is like a deck of cards, getting shuffled again. The defense doesn't take the ball away, yet it has two of the best pass rushers in the NFL on the same team. The leading rusher is a journeyman running back who just runs downhill all the time The quarterback doesn't have the protection or running game needed, but is rated statistically as one of the best in the league. The offense cannot get going in the first quarter to save its life. On Sunday, the Saints and Panthers play for first place in the NFC South in the Superdome. Admittedly, both teams have three wins in their eight games, but first place is on the line, nonetheless. It's hard to believe, but it was just 2021 that Tampa Bay , a team tied for the bottom of this division, won it all. Point being, things change rapidly in this professional sport Americans love so much. Neither of these teams is impressive in its own right, but here we stand with the mid-season top-of-the-totem position on the line. Are the Saints finally starting to find an offensive rhythm? I mean, they did score in the first quarter against Cleveland, the first time this season they've put any points in the first period column. Is the defense poised to stop the run better? They held Cleveland to under 100 yards rushing as a team, only the second time this year, the other being against the New York Giants . Is the field goal crap shoot fixed with Charlie Smyth ? The Irishman made three of four field goals last week, missing from almost 50 yards from that pesky left hash mark. There is hope, and I am going with it. Prediction: Saints 27, Panthers 21 Saints Mailbag Wednesdays, On SI Saints will answer your questions about what we see from our vantage point. To submit your thoughts or inquiries click here . The Saints have had the Panthers' number recently, but they have yet to meet this season. How will this one go? Here are the Panthers On SI staff predictions. Mark Livingston: Saints 24, Panthers 21 The Carolina Panthers have a chance to pick up a much-needed division win against the New Orleans Saints on Sunday. However, this will be a tough road test for Carolina. The Panthers need better protection for Bryce Young and a strong defensive performance under interim coordinator Todd Wash. New Orleans is coming off an overtime win against Cleveland and will look to carry that momentum into Sunday’s matchup. Expect a close game, but the Saints get the edge at home. Russell Baxter: Panthers 20, Saints 19 New Orleans Saints head coach Kellen Moore with Carolina Panthers head coach Dave Canales | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Apparently no team in the NFC South is going out of its way to want to win the title. Apparently no team in the NFC South is going out of its way to want to win the title. It’s a division where every team is at least 2 games under .500 and every club has a losing home record. A year ago, the Saints won just two games, which included a sweep of the Panthers. Bryce Young has not been super sharp as of late, but he showed a lot of resiliency last Sunday. Carolina has turned over the ball 12 times this season, but Kellen Moore’s team has been even worse. There will be a lot of bend-but-don’t-break by the Panthers’ defense, who will limit the Saints to four field goals and one touchdown, so Dave Canales’s club will eke out a one-point win. Zach Roberts: Panthers 24, Saints 23 The margins are as thin as can possibly be this Sunday. These two teams are evenly matched. The Panthers have the best win (over Detroit in Week 4), but the Saints have been better of late (coming off an OT win over the Browns). They are not separated by much. It's almost impossible to predict this one. Will the Saints' strong pass rush make mincemeat of the Panthers' weak offensive line? Will Bryce Young shred the Saints' fifth-worst pass defense? Can Tyler Shough take advantage of a depleted Panthers' secondary? Might Chuba Hubbard plow through the Saints' fourth-worst rushing defense? The Panthers have more advantages than disadvantages, and they could get back a number of healthy contributors. Still, it won't be an easy one. Preston Palm: Panthers 37, Saints 34 If there's ever a time for Carolina to get right, it’s on Sunday against the New Orleans Saints. This Saints defense is the second-worst pass defense Carolina has faced. New Orleans ranks 28th in the NFL in passing yards allowed, surrendering 236.6 per game. As an overall defense, New Orleans is arguably the worst, ranking 29th in rushing yards allowed per game. Carolina may have reinforcements coming to the defense, as EDGE Jaelan Phillips and cornerback Will Lee III are both listed as questionable for Sunday. Even if the defense underperforms, this is a game where Carolina should be able to keep up in a shootout. away.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
away.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. The Carolina Panthers and New Orleans Saints, both sitting at 3-5 on the year, will battle for first place in the NFC South division at 1 p.m. Sunday in Caesars Superdome in the heart of The Big Easy. It's a big game not only for that reason — having success against the division is paramount — but also, specifically, because of what lurks ahead for Carolina. away.headline: Panthers injury report is full of reinforcements
away.blurb: The Carolina Panthers are flailing as they try to stay afloat at the top of the ever pitiful NFC South. The team has dropped three straight games with a skeleton crew of a secondary and a revolving door of players on the offensive line. The first injury report of Week 10 brings good news though. It looks like a lot of key players are soon to return. The highlight of this injury report is all of the full participation from guys that have been out for extended periods of time. Mike Jackson, Jonathon Brooks, and Xavier Legette all had their practice windows opened on Wednesday. That doesn't guarantee that they'll be active on Sunday, but it does mean they need to be activated within the next three weeks. And the fact that they all practiced in full would suggest they're all very close to getting back to live game action. The Saints are very banged up along their offensive line. Starting center Erik McCoy is out. Both starters to his left and the backup left tackle are all dealing with their own injuries, though it doesn't seem like any will miss the game this weekend. Running back Travis Etienne is back at practice, but I wouldn't be surprised if he misses the game even after a limited practice since teams tend to be very cautious with muscle injuries like that. The Panthers (3-4) still sit atop the NFC South, but in order to hold onto their station, they’ll likely need to emerge from Bank of America Stadium with a victory against one of the powers of the AFC — the Denver Broncos (6-2). home.headline: Saints Injury Report: Tyler Shough Loses Two Key Protectors Against Panthers
home.blurb: Head coach Kellen Moore ruled out multiple players with injuries, including two starting offensive linemen: center Erik McCoy (bicep) and right tackle Taliese Fuaga (knee). The team will also miss rookie running back CJ Donaldson (shoulder) and second-round defensive lineman Christen Miller (knee). The Saints got a little more than three quarters of football out of their starting five offensive linemen last week before McCoy exited with an injury. Then Fuaga suffered a knee sprain in practice. Moore said Fuaga isn’t expected to miss enough time to land on injured reserve, but McCoy’s outlook is less certain. A few other players are questionable for Sunday’s game with the Carolina Panthers. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring) is the big name, but cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. is one to watch, too. We’ll find out for sure when the inactives list is published on Sunday. The New Orleans Saints will be short-handed in Sunday’s rivalry game with the Carolina Panthers , with the heaviest hits being on the offensive line. Saints Offensive Line Facing Major Adjustments The Saints got more than three quarters of action from their starting offensive line in last week's win over the Cleveland Browns before McCoy exited with a biceps injury. The situation worsened when Fuaga suffered a knee sprain during practice, leaving New Orleans without two important pieces of its offensive front. Moore indicated Fuaga's injury is not expected to require a stint on injured reserve, although McCoy's recovery timeline remains uncertain. McCoy's absence could prove particularly challenging as he plays a critical role in identifying defensive fronts, communicating protection adjustments and helping maintain continuity across the offensive line as the center. Without him, New Orleans must rely on Cesar Ruiz to handle those responsibilities while adjusting to a reshuffled interior with Jeremiah Wright taking Ruiz’s spot at right guard. Fuaga's injury creates another significant concern at right tackle, where Asim Richards could be called upon to step into the starting lineup. The Saints also dealt with injuries involving left tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and guard David Edwards (knee) throughout the week. While both returned to full participation Friday, it’s another sign that this unit is not even close to 100%. Even with Banks and Edwards, losing two starters makes it hard for an offensive line that has struggled with pass protection and consistency in the running game. The Buffalo Bills sit in pole position for the AFC's No. 1 seed as they visit the 2-7 New York Jets as 7. 5-point favorites at MetLife Stadium on Nov. 15, with kickoff at 1 p.m. ET on CBS. My Bills vs. Jets predictions and NFL picks expect a shootout in East Rutherford this afternoon, with neither defense providing much resistance. TOP PICK Bills vs Jets prediction today: Over 50.5 It'll take more than a short week to impact a Buffalo Bills offense that leads the league with 386.4 yards per game and 32 points per game — and this AFC East showdown with the New York Jets provides a familiar punching bag, with Buffalo scoring 30+ points in four of the last five meetings . Behind Josh Allen and James Cook , the Bills are scoring on 67% of their red-zone trips — a rate they could improve against New York's shaky run defense. The Over has also cashed in three of Buffalo's four road games this year. But this pick is about the Jets, too. Garrett Wilson 's return will fuel the New York passing game, and Geno Smith won't shy away from throwing downfield — he's completed a pass of 40+ yards in four straight games. The Over is 3-1 in the hosts' past four contests , and I'd play this up to 56%. Bills vs Jets combo After giving up 73 points over the last two games, the Jets' defense is a gift to Over bettors, and Allen has a healthy receiving corps capable of producing big plays. Buckle up for a major mismatch when the potent Buffalo ground game ( 146.6 rushing yards per game , second in the NFL) collides with a New York run defense that allows 128 rushing yards per game, ranking in the bottom 10. That paves the way for Cook to pile up carries. He's gone over this rushing attempts line in four straight games , and the Bills could lean even more heavily on the run if they build a big lead. Look for Allen to benefit, too. With nine rushing TDs already this season, he's been unstoppable near the goal line. His scrambles to escape a dangerous Jets pass rush could also carry him into the end zone. James Cook Over 19.5 rushing attempts Josh Allen anytime TD Bills vs Jets touchdown scorer: Keon Coleman There are more mouths to feed in Buffalo's offense with DJ Moore healthy again. But neither Moore nor Khalil Shakir offers the same red-zone threat as Keon Coleman , who's hauled in three touchdown catches this year. Coleman has earned Allen's trust, drawing 15 targets in his last three games , and his 6-foot-3 frame makes him a natural target on jump balls and fades. With the Bills likely to find success on the ground against a struggling Jets defense, play-action shots downfield could also create anytime TD value for Coleman. I'd play this up to 30%. Bills vs Jets player prop: Breece Hall Over 16.5 receiving yards Breece Hall has breezed past this O/U number in three straight outings , including 26 receiving yards in Kansas City last weekend. His biggest impact may come as a receiver if New York is playing catch-up. Hall has racked up 13 catches in his four contests this season. While the Bills strengthened their secondary with the trade for Amani Hooker, the Jets' downfield threats can open up the middle of the field for Hall to do damage. I'd play this up to 18.5 and 56%. away.headline: Bills starting tackle misses practice as four offensive linemen deal with injuries
away.blurb: Starting right tackle Spencer Brown was the only Bills player who did not practice Thursday because of an ankle injury. Brown was listed as a limited participant during Wednesday's walkthrough, when practice participation was estimated. The Bills have four starting offensive linemen on their injury report, including left tackle Dion Dawkins (rib), left guard Alec Anderson (ankle) and center Connor McGovern (neck). All three were limited Wednesday and Thursday. Buffalo also listed cornerback Christian Benford as a limited participant for the second consecutive day because of a wrist injury . Benford injured his right wrist against Minnesota, underwent an X-ray at halftime and returned before leaving again in the third quarter. Tight end Dalton Kincaid (ankle) was limited Wednesday and Thursday, while defensive tackle Greg Gaines (calf) was a full participant both days after missing two consecutive games. Defensive back Sam Franklin Jr . was added to Thursday's injury report with a shoulder injury and was limited. Wide receiver Garrett Wilson was limited for the second consecutive day because of a concussion that forced him to miss Sunday's loss to the Kansas City Chiefs. Defensive tackle Harrison Phillips (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) did not practice for the second consecutive day. Now four starters are dealing with injuries heading into Sunday's game against the New York Jets. Dawkins and Anderson missed Buffalo's 23-6 victory over the Minnesota Vikings on Monday Night Football. Tylan Grable started at left tackle, while Austin Corbett filled in at left guard. Brown returned against Minnesota after missing Buffalo's previous game against Baltimore because of a back injury. The Bills (7-1) visit the Jets (2-7) at 1 p.m. Sunday, Nov. 15, at MetLife Stadium. The Jets have multiple several injury concerns. Cornerback Jarvis Brownlee Jr. was also absent Thursday because of an illness. Both teams will release their final injury reports Friday, including game status designations for Sunday's game.

home.headline: Jets get major Garrett Wilson injury update from Aaron Glenn
home.blurb: His return would put him and Breece Hall on the field together for quarterback Geno Smith, something that hasn’t happened since Week 3. Hall, a running back, rejoined the lineup last week following a five-game absence with an injured quadriceps. Wilson got hurt against Las Vegas in the game before the Kansas City trip. He missed practice entirely the following week, sat out the Chiefs game and was limited in two sessions since. Omar Cooper Jr., a rookie receiver, was limited all week by an ankle injury but should play too. That gives the Jets Wilson, Cooper, Adonai Mitchell and Isaiah Williams at receiver, with every one of their tight ends available. On defense, edge rusher Joseph Ossai, defensive lineman Harrison Phillips and cornerbacks Jarvis Brownlee Jr. and Nahshon Wright should all be available, per Glenn. Backup linebacker Trevin Wallace won’t play due to a groin injury. Garrett Wilson sits a single concussion protocol step away from returning, and New York Jets coach Aaron Glenn believes the wide receiver will clear it before facing the Buffalo Bills . Wilson leads the 2-7 Jets with 43 catches for 527 yards and three touchdowns, and New York has dropped four straight heading into a Week 10 meeting with a Bills club that shares the league’s top record, 7-1, alongside San Francisco. Glenn explained where things stand with his top wideout. “Garrett still has one more step to go through before he’s cleared,” Glenn said . “And I see that happening.” Asked whether he expected Wilson to suit up against Buffalo, the coach didn’t hedge. “I am confident in that,” Glenn said. Those numbers came amid his frustration over how inconsistently offensive coordinator Frank Reich has used him. Reich and Glenn have both said they’d work on fixing that. Buffalo ranks first leaguewide in scoring and total yards, so New York may need Wilson to help it trade points. New York still has to release one more injury report before the Bills game, and that one will carry official designations. away.headline: Seahawks’ Mike Macdonald Gives Strong Jalen Milroe Statement Amid QB Injuries
away.blurb: As for Milroe, the first-team repetitions are a chance to show he can handle more than a limited package constructed around his athleticism. Seattle will start Lock against the Las Vegas Raiders on Sunday, Nov. 15, with Darnold ruled out because of quadriceps and rib injuries. The veteran has been limited in practice while managing an elbow injury and the oblique issue he suffered against the Arizona Cardinals. Klint Kubiak Speaks out on Facing Seahawks in Week 10 Seahawks' Mike Macdonald Gives Strong Jalen Milroe Statement Amid QB Injuries Unlock the latest Heavy on Seahawks news — direct to your inbox. The Seattle Seahawks have spent the past two weeks dealing with injuries to their top two quarterbacks. That's given Jalen Milroe more time with the starting offense. And head coach Mike Macdonald likes what he has seen. Speaking with reporters Friday, Nov. 13, Macdonald delivered strong praise for the second-year quarterback's work while Drew Lock and Sam Darnold recover from injuries. "I think it's appropriate to say Jalen has done a tremendous job when he's been in there with the ones," Macdonald said. The coach went on to laud Milroe's work ethic, accuracy and decision-making. He specifically highlighted the young quarterback's ability to deliver throws on time. It's a welcome assessment for a player who has waited for a chance to show his ability for much of his NFL career. Seahawks' Jalen Milroe Impresses Mike Macdonald With First-Team Offense Milroe has taken snaps with Seattle's starters during the past two weeks as Lock works through elbow and oblique injuries. Macdonald made it obvious Friday that the extra work hasn't been wasted. The coach described Milroe as decisive with the football and praised his execution when called upon to replace Lock during practice. The comments came in a Nov. 13 report from Seahawks.com's John Boyle . Seattle selected Milroe in the third round of the 2025 NFL draft, taking the former Alabama quarterback with the No. 92 overall pick. His rookie season showed very little game experience. Milroe appeared in three regular-season contests, carrying the ball three times for four yards without attempting a pass. Heading into 2026, he sat behind Darnold and Lock on the depth chart The latest injuries have changed his practice workload, though they haven't produced an official quarterback change. Still, Macdonald put forth confidence Friday that Lock can handle another start, so Milroe is an important insurance option. If Lock cannot finish Sunday's game, Seattle could be forced to turn to the former Alabama standout against Las Vegas. Milroe has now prepared for that possibility for weeks. away.headline: Week 10 Injury Report: Seahawks at Raiders
away.blurb: The Seahawks will be getting a couple of players back from injury for Sunday's game in Las Vegas, with outside linebacker Uchenna Nwosu and receiver Rashid Shaheed both ready to return after missing the past two games with ankle and knee injuries, respectively. The Seahawks will still be without four players who also missed last week's game: left tackle Charles Cross (ankle), quarterback Sam Darnold (ribs/quadriceps), guard Quenton Nelson (knee) and defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger), all of whom were ruled out on Friday's injury report. Cross, who was able to practice Thursday on a limited basis, should be able to make it back after Seattle's Week 11 bye, Seahawks coach Mike Macdonald said. Quarterback Drew Lock was limited all week due to elbow and oblique injuries, as was expected coming into the week, but he has no injury designation, and the plan is still for him to make his second straight start in place of Darnold. Defensive tackle Jarran Reed , who did not practice Wednesday or Thursday due to a personal matter, was back at practice Friday and will play, Macdonald said, clarifying that it was a good personal matter. For the Raiders, defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and receiver Dont'e Thornton (back), are listed as questionable. The only other changes were that tight end AJ Barner , who was a full participant Wednesday with a finger injury, has been removed from the injury report altogether, and Jaxon Smith-Njigba , who got a rest day on Wednesday, was a full participant. As expected, quarterback Drew Lock was limited again, as has been the plan as he prepares to start while dealing with elbow and oblique injuries. Defensive tackle Leonard Williams , who is dealing with a stinger, was a non-participant for the second day in a row, as were quarterback Sam Darnold and left guard Quenton Nelson , both of whom have already been ruled out of Week 10 by Mike Macdonald. home.headline: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns
home.blurb: Seahawks-Raiders Wednesday injury report: Leonard Williams still out, Rashid Shaheed returns - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Seattle released the first of the three weekly injury reports, which is headlined by the health of backup quarterback Drew Lock, who is battling a lingering elbow injury and a new oblique injury. Lock was limited in practice on Wednesday, with head coach Mike Macdonald indicating that the veteran is "making good progress" and may start against the Raiders. Whoever is under center will once again be working with a patchwork offensive line as stars Quenton Nelson and Charles Cross did not practice. Nelson is battling a knee injury that might hold him out for his second straight game while Cross has been out with an ankle injury since Week 7. Backup guard Anthony Bradford continues to be hampered by a knee injury and was limited on Wednesday. On the defensive side, Leonard Williams remains out with a stinger that he suffered against the Kansas City Chiefs, and edge rusher Derick Hall was limited with a new back injury. Both would be a massive loss for the Seahawks front that will hope to ruin Raiders' rookie Fernando Mendoza's debut. It wasn't all negative for the Seahawks' defense, though, as signs are trending positive for edge rusher Uchenna Nwosu, who was limited with the ankle injury that's held him out of the team's last two games. away.headline: Is Myles Garrett playing today? Latest on Rams star's Week 10 status
away.blurb: The Los Angeles Rams enter today's game with five players listed as questionable to play, including star edge rusher Myles Garrett . After missing seven straight games, Garrett returned to the starting lineup last week for the Rams, recording three sacks and a forced fumble in a win over the Washington Commanders . Garrett was limited in the first two practices of the week and then was held out on Friday as part of a veteran rest day. He's officially listed as questionable due to a lingering knee injury, though there isn't much concern about the reigning Defensive Player of the Year. Garrett is questionable but he's expected to play, according to Sean McVay. Before practice on Friday, McVay told reporters that Garrett is expected to play, saying that he's "feeling good." "Myles Garrett, he'll be questionable for the game. He's feeling good. It's more of just getting him feeling as good as possible. He's had a really good week, played a bunch of snaps and we expect him to be able to build on that, but we're being smart with him," McVay said. Is Myles Garrett playing today? When asked if he expects Garrett to play Sunday, McVay said, "I do." There hasn't been an update since, so the expectation is that Garrett will suit up. home.headline: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals
home.blurb: Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals - Yahoo Sports Search Query for Search Search Home News Finance Sports More Mail NFL Rams Injury Report: Myles Garrett, Trent McDuffie Questionable vs. Cardinals The Los Angeles Rams will be managing several injuries on Sunday as they take on the Arizona Cardinals for the second time this season in Week 10. While wide receiver Puka Nacua went on injured reserve this week , left guard Steve Avila has been ruled out as well. Additionally, after making his return in Week 9 against the Washington Commanders, Myles Garrett has officially been listed as questionable but is expected to play, according to head coach Sean McVay. In addition to Garrett, tight end Davis Allen, long snapper Joe Cardona, cornerback Trent McDuffie, and safety Kam Curl were all listed as questionable. After being a non-participant in practice on Thursday, Allen was limited in Friday's practice. With Colby Parkinson not having an injury designation, the Rams should be in a good spot at tight end if Allen is able to go. More importantly, the Rams will be looking to get McDuffie back in action. He was a non-participant in practice on Thursday but was upgraded to limited on Friday. After returning against the Los Angeles Chargers in Week 8, McDuffie missed last week's game against the Commanders and has been nursing a back injury. "A lot of it is going to be contingent upon how that limited work goes today. He was rolling, doing a lot of good stuff yesterday," McVay said. "He's chomping at the bit to play, but a lot of that answer will be predicated on how he handles the physical workload today. I think if you asked him, he would say that he's hopeful to be able to play and so are we, but that could change based on how the workout goes." Without Nacua on Sunday, the Rams will be relying heavily on their wide receiver depth . The Rams signed Xavier Smith back to the roster this week and also added Brennan Presley to the active roster. With Avila out as well, Beaux Limmer will likely take his spot at left guard. While the Rams are hoping to get McDuffie back, if he is out, the Rams will rely on Emmanuel Forbes and Josh Wallace for a second straight week. On the Cardinals' side of things, defensive lineman Zach Carter, center Hjalte Froholdt, and interior offensive lineman Jon Gaines have all been ruled out. Additionally, tight end Hunter Long, cornerback Max Melton, offensive lineman Jayden Williams, safety Andrew Wingard, defensive lineman Roy Lopez, and defensive lineman Darius Robinson are all questionable. away.headline: 49ers vs. Cowboys injury report: 2 starting corners continue to miss practice
away.blurb: The good news is that ESPN's Nick Wagoner noted that it sounded like Lenoir and Green participated in Thursday morning's walkthrough, which the media could not observe. That suggests that both might be trending towards being available on Sunday. During his Thursday interview on Bay Area radio station KNBR, head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether Lenoir and Green need to practice to play in a game. The question was about Green and cornerback Upton Stout , but the latter was likely mentioned by mistake instead of Lenoir, as Stout has been practicing—albeit as a limited participant—this week. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel returned to practice Wednesday after missing three games with a hamstring injury. He was back on the field Thursday, putting him closer to a potential return against Dallas. It's also worth noting that linebacker Dre Greenlaw and tackle Trent Williams were limited participants. Greenlaw is listed with a knee injury, while Williams is dealing with a shoulder issue. Neither practiced on Wednesday, which was designated a rest day for both. This may be something to keep an eye on this week. away.blurb: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams sustained a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss his third consecutive game, but Deebo Samuel is expected to return for the 49ers on Sunday. The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. “It’s been going well,” Shanahan said. “I’m sure if this was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction.” Left tackle Trent Williams is listed as questionable with a shoulder condition. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams injured his shoulder Thursday in practice. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw sustained a knee injury in practice Thursday, too. He is also listed as questionable. The 49ers have a bit of uncertainty at cornerback, too. Starters Renardo Green (back), Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) are listed as questionable against the Cowboys. The 49ers could also activate defensive tackle CJ West (knee) off the injured reserve list. He is listed as questionable. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton went on injured reserve this week after sustaining a fractured and dislocated ankle. By Matt Maiocco, 49ers Insider • Published November 13, 2026 • Updated on November 13, 2026 at 2:46 pm The 49ers should get a further boost at wide receiver with the addition of veteran Keenan Allen, who will make his San Francisco debut after arriving in a midweek trade from the Indianapolis Colts. “He’ll have a role,” 49ers coach Kyle Shanahan said of Allen. The 49ers acquired Allen at a time when the team has experienced an abundance of injuries at wide receiver. That list includes Evans, who left the Oct. 19 game against Washington due to Achilles tendinitis. With the Colts still in mind, Dallas faces the possibility of facing the same receiver for the second week in a row. After dressing for Indianapolis, wideout Keenan Allen has the rare opportunity to face the same opponent two weeks in a row after the veteran receiver was shipped to the 49ers just before the NFL trade deadline. This past offseason, Dallas shipped interior defensive lineman Osa Odighizuwa to the Bay Area prompting some to wonder if the Cowboys traded the wrong defensive tackle to what looks like a superior opponent. That suggests that both might be trending towards being available on Sunday. During his Thursday interview on Bay Area radio station KNBR, head coach Kyle Shanahan was asked whether Lenoir and Green need to practice to play in a game. The question was about Green and cornerback Upton Stout , but the latter was likely mentioned by mistake instead of Lenoir, as Stout has been practicing—albeit as a limited participant—this week. Wide receiver Deebo Samuel returned to practice Wednesday after missing three games with a hamstring injury. He was back on the field Thursday, putting him closer to a potential return against Dallas. It's also worth noting that linebacker Dre Greenlaw and tackle Trent Williams were limited participants. Greenlaw is listed with a knee injury, while Williams is dealing with a shoulder issue. Neither practiced on Wednesday, which was designated a rest day for both. As a result, the Cowboys have been forced to look for some reinforcements and have turned to the practice squad to bring in a familiar face. On Saturday, the Cowboys signed tight end James Mitchell from the practice squad to the active roster as part of a flurry of roster moves . The 27-year-old as released by the Panthers as part of the final roster cuts ahead of the 2026-27 season, before getting signed to the Cowboys practice squad a few days later. home.blurb: 49ers injury report: Deebo cleared, Trent Williams questionable – NBC Sports Bay Area & California Warriors San Francisco 49ers left tackle Trent Williams sustained a shoulder injury during Thursday's practice and is questionable for Sunday's game in Dallas. Wide receiver Mike Evans will miss his third consecutive game, but Deebo Samuel is expected to return for the 49ers on Sunday. The 49ers fully cleared Samuel to return for the team’s Week 10 game against the Dallas Cowboys. He has not played since Oct. 11, when he sustained a hamstring injury in a Week 5 win over the Seattle Seahawks. “It’s been going well,” Shanahan said. “I’m sure if this was the last game or something, he’d be able to go out there. But we’re just trying to make sure it fully heals so it doesn’t act up again. But it’s going in the right direction.” Left tackle Trent Williams is listed as questionable with a shoulder condition. Coach Kyle Shanahan said Williams injured his shoulder Thursday in practice. Linebacker Dre Greenlaw sustained a knee injury in practice Thursday, too. He is also listed as questionable. The 49ers have a bit of uncertainty at cornerback, too. Starters Renardo Green (back), Deommodore Lenoir (foot) and nickel back Upton Stout (shoulder) are listed as questionable against the Cowboys. The 49ers could also activate defensive tackle CJ West (knee) off the injured reserve list. He is listed as questionable. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton went on injured reserve this week after sustaining a fractured and dislocated ankle. LogoParamountPlus More live games and exclusives Log Out Connect TV Provider More live games & exclusives Log Out Connect NFL News & Highlights Pittsburgh won the first matchup between the two teams back in Week 3 Getty Images The 10th Sunday of the 2026 NFL regular season will conclude with the Pittsburgh Steelers and Cincinnati Bengals battling for first place in the AFC North division. Pittsburgh (6-2) currently leads the North by virtue of its Week 5 win over Cincinnati (6-2). The Steelers have won seven of the last nine games between the two teams dating back to the start of the 2022 season. The second of those two losses occurred the last time these two teams played in Cincinnati. Last October, Cincinnati won a 33-31 shootout. The Steelers won the rematch a month later in Pittsburgh. Here's how you can follow the action in real time. We've also included a breakdown and a prediction for Sunday night's showdown. Where to watch Bengals vs. Steelers live When: Sunday, Nov. 15 | Time: 8:20 p.m. ET Where: Paycor Stadium -- Cincinnati, Ohio TV: NBC | Stream: fubo (try for free) Follow: CBS Sports App Odds: Bengals -3.5, O/U 47.5 (via DraftKings ) Bengals vs. Steelers: Need to know Last time we met The Steelers sealed a 30-27 win when Derrick Harmon strip-sacked Joe Burrow on the Bengals' final series. Cincinnati was in field goal range when the turnover occurred. Jaylen Warren was the catalyst for Pittsburgh's win. The fifth-year veteran rushed for 127 yards on 17 carries and caught three passes for 49 yards. Warren's success helped open things up for Aaron Rodgers , who threw for 292 yards and three touchdowns with one interception. Rodgers was able to top Burrow, who threw for 282 yards and three touchdowns. Red hot teams Both Pittsburgh and Cincinnati come into this game with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers went into their Week 9 bye with a 27-6 win over the Browns . Cincinnati is coming off a 34-27 win over the Falcons in Madrid, Spain. It'll be interesting to see how much the previous week will impact Sunday night's game. The Bengals may still be feeling the effects of traveling overseas. The Steelers, meanwhile, are rested and might be getting back some key players who have missed time with injuries. One of those players is Harmon, who has missed time with a foot injury. Reasons for success Pittsburgh's success has been powered by Warren (and, to a lesser degree, fellow running back Rico Dowdle , who has played well in a complementary role since returning from his injury in Week 6) and a defense that hasn't allowed a touchdown in seven quarters. Pittsburgh is once again getting high-level play from T.J. Watt , who has already eclipsed his 2025 sack tally. Cincinnati's current winning streak has largely been the byproduct of Burrow (who leads the NFL in completion percentage and touchdown passes) and his success throwing to Ja'Marr Chase and Tee Higgins . The Bengals have also received solid play from a defense that is getting big contributions from offseason acquisitions Dexter Lawrence and Boye Mafe . Prediction, pick This game will come down to two things: Pittsburgh's ability to throw the ball (which would in turn help open things up for the running game) and Cincinnati's ability to keep Burrow clean, which has at times been an issue against the Steelers. The Bengals want to make this a shootout, while the Steelers will want to play keep-away while keeping Burrow and Co. on the sideline. While Pittsburgh's plan can in theory work, its lack of depth at the receiver position might come back to haunt them on Sunday night. In close matchups like this, special teams can often make the difference. If that ends up being the case in this game, the Bengals have the advantage in Evan McPherson , who has not missed a field goal or an extra point this season. Conversely, Steelers kicker Chris Boswell has already missed field goals this season. Taking on the Cincinnati Bengals, the Steelers can take the season series against their rival while earning their seventh victory of the season. After a bye week, the team is hoping to shake off the cobwebs before Week 10 action begins. It’s the middle of the regular season schedule, but there is a playoff atmosphere to this matchup. The Steelers can get their seventh win of the year, and a few of these bold predictions might come true as well. Alex Highsmith’s Career Day It’s been a little too quiet for veteran outside linebacker Alex Highsmith. He recorded 0.5 sacks in the team’s latest win, but he hasn’t recorded an individual sack since Week 2 against the New England Patriots. His previous in-game highs are 11 tackles and 3.0 sacks. Against the Bengals this week, Highsmith breaks the tackles record and posts multiple sacks. Jaylen Warren Records Two Receiving Touchdowns Jaylen Warren is the best piece of the Steelers’ offense, and It’s undeniable. He’s one of the best running backs in the NFL this season and he’s single-handedly carried this offense at times. What he hasn’t done, however, is consistently find the endzone. He has just two rushing touchdowns and one receiving touchdown on the season, with two of his total scores coming in the same contest against the Indianapolis Colts. That changes in Week 10. Against the Bengals, I predict Warren will dominate both out of the backfield and as a receiving threat. As a receiver is where I believe he will do his most damage, finding the end zone twice on passing plays. The Bengals might have a plan to limit Warren on the ground, but that’s not enough to keep him from making an impact. Mandatory Credit: Charles LeClaire-Imagn Images | IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect Steelers Stifle Bengals on 3rd Down Steelers Stifle Bengals on 3rd Down One area the Bengals have been so successful on offense is converting on third down. It doesn’t matter if they have significant yardage to gain, they tend to convert. Senior NFL researcher Tony Holzman-Escareno shared an interesting statistic recently that sheds light on this specifically. The Bengals are the NFL leaders at converting on third down whenever they have at least seven yards to gain. When they are facing a third and long situation like that, the Bengals are picking up the first down 39.5% of the time. It leads the next-best team, the San Francisco 49ers, by nearly 5%. Highest 3rd & long (7+ yards) conversion rate this season: 1. Bengals – 39.5% 2. 49ers – 34.6% 3. Raiders – 31.4% 4. Panthers – 30.0% 5. Jaguars – 29.2% 6. Bills - 28.9% 7. Seahawks – 28.8% 8. Bears – 28.6% 9. Chiefs – 28.2% 10. Lions – 27.9% Lowest: 28. Vikings – 18.5%… The Steelers are likely to put the Bengals in third and long situations throughout Week 10. The only difference between Cincinnati’s previous success and this matchup, is Pittsburgh's pass rush. While the Bengals lead the league in pass touchdowns and third and long conversions, the Steelers are the best team when it comes to taking down the quarterback. It's a matchup of two unstoppable forces, and I'm betting on Pittsburgh's pass rush to limit Joey B and the Bengals to less than a 20% success rate on third down.
