away.headline: Justin Herbert Injured, DJ Uiagalelei Makes NFL Debut as Chargers Fall to 0-8 in Loss to Texans
away.blurb: "Could be a fracture, we'll find out," Harbaugh told reporters after the game on Sunday. The Chargers quarterback, who went undrafted out of Florida State, came in for Herbert late in the fourth quarter as his team trailed big. The prospect of Uiagalelei taking the starting job from Herbert would have sounded like a joke coming into the season, but nothing is out of the realm of possibility amid an 0-8 start. Los Angeles Chargers quarterback Justin Herbert avoided a fractured finger after suffering an injury during Sunday's 44-22 loss to the Houston Texans, coach Jim Harbaugh revealed on Monday. Harbaugh said on Sunday that Herbert wanted to finish the game, but the coaching staff thought better of it. Herbert said he will do "whatever I can to make sure I'm 100 percent." While Harbaugh noted Herbert wanted to play through the injury, the coach opted to have DJ Uiagalelei—who made his NFL debut on Sunday—finish the game. Uiagalelei's first drive ended with a touchdown pass. Uiagalelei finished his first NFL game with 24 yards and a touchdown on 2-of-7 passing. It had been another rough day for Herbert before he exited, as he had just 193 yards, a touchdown and an interception. Herbert came into the game with 1,398 passing yards, five touchdowns and 10 interceptions. Before Sunday, he hadn't thrown a touchdown pass since Week 5. The Chargers' hopes of reaching the playoffs are essentially over at this point, but bringing in a new starting quarterback could give the team a spark heading into the second half of the season. Uiagalelei had a five-year college career with Clemson, Oregon State and Florida State, though he never quite lived up to the hype he had coming into college. After going undrafted in 2025, he signed with the Chargers but didn't make the 53-man roster. He spent last season on the team's practice squad. Over the offseason, he competed for the backup position behind Herbert but ultimately lost to Trey Lance and started the year on the practice squad. After Lance was placed on the injured reserve with a groin injury in September, Uiagalelei was promoted to the active roster, paving the way for him to serve as Herbert's backup.

away.headline: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report
away.blurb: Move Over Substation, Chargers Have a New King of Injuries in LA with Week 10 Report Skip to main content SI.COM The Los Angeles Chargers are 0-8, they just had a final hour trade before the trade deadline fall through and they are still searching for any sort of identity on offense. Los Angeles has been dealing with injuries all season long, by Week Six they already had over half of their original 53-man roster on the injury report or injured reserve. The Chargers injury luck is not improving much. For all the jokes and talk about the electrical substation near the San Francisco 49ers practice facility, Los Angeles may have something worse. The Chargers' practice facility, the Bolt, is located near Los Angeles International Airport, perhaps it's the air quality, or something in the the Los Angeles water or perhaps SoFi Stadium itself, something is up in LA. The Rams, who now have placed another wide receiver on injured reserve, may agree SoFi stadium, the Chargers and Rams' shared stadium, has a role in this. Both Los Angeles teams are in the top 10 of most injured this season in nearly every metric. The Chargers emerge from the NFL trade deadline with the exact same roster and will now head to Baltimore to take on the Jacoby Brissett-led Ravens on Monday Night Football. The Chargers will have a chance to steal their first win of the season as the Ravens search for their identity with a brand new quarterback at the helm but will their long list of injuries get in the way? thursday's injury report for week 10 at BAL pic.twitter.com/fXSvi1MmEt It feels like groundhog day for the Chargers and their MASH unit of players following their loss to the Houston Texans. The Chargers have a significant portion of their cornerback room on the injury report. Tarheeb Still and Donte Jackson are the only cornerbacks not on the injury report to start the week of practice. The Chargers offensive line continues to be cursed. Guards Kayode Awosika, Alex Harkey and Branson Taylor are all on the injury report and Taylor was unable to practice at all after getting his first snaps of the season against Houston. Wide receivers Ladd McConkey and Tre' Harris are both on the report with McConkey missing the first practice of the week following suffering back spasms during pregame warmups prior to the week nine matchup against the Texans. The Chargers have had a revolving door at most positions on offense this season, which certainly has not helped their performance. As the Chargers, offensive coordinator Mike McDaniel and quarterback Justin Herbert continue to try to dial in the offense, their efforts are clearly made more of a challenge with the amount of injuries facing the unit. home.headline: New Lamar Jackson Rumors Update When Ravens QB Had Surgery amid Latest Injury Timeline for Return
home.blurb: Baltimore Ravens star quarterback Lamar Jackson has a chance to return this season based on when he had thumb surgery. "He is doing everything he can to get back, and we will let his progress guide the timing of his return," Minter said. "We are committed to playing our best football over the second half of the season." Per ESPN's Adam Schefter , Jackson's surgery happened last week so based on the estimated recovery time of six to 10 weeks, he could potentially be back on the field before the regular season ends. Ravens head coach Jesse Minter said in a statement on Nov. 13 that Jackson's recovery timeline was "challenging to predict" after he underwent surgery to address a dislocated and broken right thumb. A six-week recovery would have Jackson back around Week 15 when the Ravens play the Pittsburgh Steelers. The full 10-week timeline would give him a chance to play in Week 18, also against the Steelers. In addition to his hand injury, Jackson also missed three games earlier in the year after suffering a high ankle sprain. In five games, he played just 14 full quarters and threw for 961 yards, six touchdowns and one interception while adding 144 rushing yards and another score. In the wake of Jackson's injury, the Ravens traded for veteran quarterback Jacoby Brissett, who is expected to make his first start for the team against the Los Angeles Chargers on Monday Night Football in Week 10. At 4-5, Baltimore has work to do if it hopes to make the playoffs. The Ravens will likely remain cautious with Jackson's recovery, making the acquisition of Brissett a critical move as they look to snap their four-game losing streak going into Monday night.

home.headline: Ravens reveal Lamar Jackson injury timeline that might not end his season
home.blurb: Huntley is out for the remainder of the 2026 NFL season, and Jackson's injury was also seen as season-ending. But ahead of Week 10, the Ravens shared some big news. The 5-4 Ravens will need a lot of things to go their way, including Jackson's recovery going well. But even if it takes the full 10 weeks, as Minter revealed in the statement, Jackson could return in the first round of the playoffs, or in Week 18. There is still a lot of uncertainty when it comes to Jackson returning for the Ravens, but just hearing that he has a chance to return at some point this season, after the doom and gloom a few weeks ago, is some very positive news for the Ravens. home.headline: Chargers Drop Big Trey Pipkins Injury Update Ahead of Ravens
home.blurb: According to Aaron Wilson, the Chargers officially designated OL Trey Pipkins to return from Injury Reserve. Meaning Pipkins gets a 21-day practice window to return from injured reserve on Thursday, which is huge news for an offensive line missing Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, and Trevor Penning on IR. Trey Pipkins Set to Return from IR Pipkins is already 30, and an elongated absence might force the Chargers to cut him, given how dire their situation is. The 2019 third-round pick, No. 91 overall out of Sioux Falls, has started 10 games for L.A. in 2025 before re-signing on a two-year, $10 million contract in March 2026. It runs through 2028, so the Chargers are likely to give him some time still. But it's the Chargers' offensive urgency that makes his return that much more important. The entire Chargers' offensive line has been hammered by injuries all year, Rashawn Slater, Tyler Biadasz, and Trevor Penning all on IR, plus guard Kayode Awosika (fibula) limited in practice this week.
